items.title: Achraf Hakimi prévient l’Europe : le PSG veut conserver sa couronne continentale
items.description: Après le succès du Paris Saint-Germain face au FC Barcelone (4-2) en Ligue des champions, Achraf Hakimi a réaffirmé les ambitions du club parisien. Le latéral marocain estime que son équipe a les moyens de continuer à dominer l’Europe et vise un troisième sacre consécutif dans la compétition. Le Paris Saint-Germain a envoyé un signal fort à ses concurrents européens. Vainqueurs du FC Barcelone sur le score de 4-2, mardi soir au Parc des Princes, les Parisiens ont signé une nouvelle performance de référence après avoir également pris le dessus sur Manchester City une semaine auparavant. À l’issue de cette rencontre spectaculaire, Achraf Hakimi n’a pas caché sa satisfaction. Pour l’international marocain, ce succès illustre la capacité du PSG à répondre présent face aux grandes équipes européennes et à assumer son statut de champion. « Nous voulons montrer que nous sommes les champions et que nous voulons continuer à gagner » , a expliqué le défenseur parisien, qui considère son équipe comme l’une des meilleures du monde actuellement. Face à un FC Barcelone jusque-là invaincu cette saison, les joueurs de Luis Enrique ont dû faire preuve de caractère. Malgré les égalisations catalanes et les difficultés rencontrées au cours du match, le PSG a su trouver les ressources nécessaires pour faire la différence. Hakimi a notamment insisté sur l’intensité exigée par ce type de confrontation, où la rigueur défensive compte autant que la capacité à se montrer dangereux en attaque. Il a également salué la qualité de l’adversaire, tout en soulignant la force collective de son équipe. Pour le Marocain, cette victoire ne constitue pas une fin en soi. Le club parisien entend poursuivre sur cette lancée et défendre son titre européen avec une ambition clairement affichée. Le latéral du PSG a également évoqué l’objectif majeur de la saison : remporter une nouvelle Ligue des champions. Après deux sacres consécutifs, les Parisiens veulent prolonger leur règne continental et inscrire un peu plus leur nom dans l’histoire de la compétition. Hakimi attribue une partie de cette ambition au travail quotidien de Luis Enrique, qui veille à entretenir l’état d’esprit conquérant de son groupe. Selon lui, le technicien espagnol pousse ses joueurs à maintenir un niveau d’exigence élevé et à ne jamais se satisfaire des résultats déjà obtenus. The post Achraf Hakimi prévient l’Europe : le PSG veut conserver sa couronne continentale appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Cross River State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, endorsing the proposed establishment of state police to address insecurity through a decentralised policing system. All 22 lawmakers present at plenary voted in favour of the bill, with none opposing it. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. Ayambem, however, stressed that the implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, said policing must be brought closer to the people. He argued that a decentralised system would improve security responses and enable law enforcement agencies to address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies to ensure that the proposed State Police Services complemented existing security structures and improved overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, emphasised the need for adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism in the proposed system. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect citizens’ fundamental rights. Lawmakers also identified improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as potential benefits of decentralised policing. The passage marks the Cross River Assembly’s endorsement of the proposed constitutional amendments. The bill must proceed through the constitutionally prescribed amendment process before the proposed changes can take effect nationally. items.title: Man arrested after allegedly taping wife to chair to watch football ‘in peace’
items.description: A 64-year-old Richmond man is facing serious legal consequences after he reportedly bound his wife to a chair with tape and left her in their basement so he could watch a football game upstairs without interruption. The suspect, identified as Terry Ward, was taken into custody following a late-night domestic disturbance call at a residence in the 2200 block of Maplewood Avenue in Richmond. According to a Richmond Police Department criminal complaint obtained by Virginia Statewide Incidents, officers arrived at the scene around 11:30 p.m. to investigate a domestic dispute. Responding officers took a statement from an adult female who detailed a harrowing 30 to 45-minute ordeal. She told investigators that her husband had forcibly restrained her to a chair in the basement using tape. The responding officer noted in the complaint that the physical evidence heavily backed her claim, documenting visible marks and sticky tape residue around both of the woman’s arms. According to the official court documents, investigators secured an outright admission from the suspect at the scene. The officer explicitly wrote in the criminal complaint that Ward stated he “did indeed tie his wife to a chair and place her down in the basement.” Sources familiar with the case confirmed that while his wife remained trapped downstairs, Ward went back upstairs to watch the game in complete isolation. Following the police response, Ward was arrested and formally charged with felony abduction and misdemeanour assault on a family member. Online records from the Richmond Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court indicate that his next formal court appearance is scheduled for November 10, 2026. items.title: Monrovia set for AWBL Zone 3 qualifying showdown
items.description: The race for two places in the final rounds of the African Women’s Basketball League (AWBL) will take centre stage in Monrovia, Liberia as six clubs prepare to compete in the FIBA Africa Zone 3 qualifiers from November 2 to 9, 2026. With the competition set for the Samuel Kanyon Doe (SKD) Indoor Gymnasium in Paynesville, the participating teams face a demanding week in which every result could prove decisive in their quest to reach the continental finals in Cairo, Egypt, scheduled for December 11–19. Liberia will have two representatives in the contest, with Flames Basketball Club, the domestic league runners-up, joined by reigning national champions D’Rockers Basketball Club. Both sides will be eager to make home advantage count against a competitive field. Côte d’Ivoire’s Friends of Basketball Association (FBA), the defending FIBA Africa Zone 3 champions, will arrive with a title to defend, while Benin Republic’s Energie Basketball Club of Cotonou brings its experience from previous appearances in the competition. Nigeria’s Mountain of Fire Ministries (MFM) Basketball Club and First Bank Basketball Club complete the six-team lineup, setting up another chapter in one of the country’s notable domestic rivalries. MFM heads to Liberia with bragging rights after edging First Bank 66–64 in the Zenith Bank Women’s Basketball League final at the Indoor Sports Hall of the National Stadium. The closely fought encounter, played before a packed arena, underlined how little separates the two Nigerian sides. Their meeting in Monrovia could therefore carry added significance, as both clubs seek to translate their domestic form into continental success and secure passage to Cairo. The Nigerian representatives were able to enter the qualifiers after FIBA Africa and the Liberia Basketball Association (LBA) extended the registration deadline and adjusted the competition schedule. The changes followed an intervention by FIBA Africa Zone 3 President, Colonel Sam Ahmedu (Rtd), enabling both clubs to participate after the late conclusion of their domestic league campaign. Preparations in Liberia are also gathering momentum. Calvin Diggs, president of Flames Basketball Club and Secretary-General of the LBA, told FIRST ZEALMEDIACAST BLOG in a telephone interview from Monrovia that they are working to ensure a smooth and successful event. According to Diggs, the Organizing Committee and the LBA have intensified preparations, with the goal of delivering a competition that meets international standards. FIBA Africa Zone 3 Secretary Joe Apu also expressed confidence in Liberia’s readiness, pointing to the experience accumulated by the country’s basketball community through hosting several international events in recent years. As the countdown continues, the six clubs are reportedly reinforcing their squads ahead of the showdown. The immediate objective for the teams are clear, finish among the top two and earn the opportunity to compete for the AWBL title in Egypt. With the defending zonal champions, two Nigerian rivals, experienced Beninese contenders and a determined Liberian challenge all in the mix, the Monrovia qualifiers promise a compelling test of depth, consistency and ambition.

items.title: Dix suspects interpellés dans une affaire présumée de réseau QNET
items.description: La Brigade territoriale de Sangalkam a interpellé dix ressortissants étrangers, le lundi 19 octobre 2026, à Kounoune Centrale, au Sénégal, à la suite d’un renseignement signalant la présence présumée d’un réseau lié à QNET. Les investigations se poursuivent pour déterminer l’étendue des activités de ce réseau et établir les responsabilités des personnes mises en cause. L’opération menée par la Brigade territoriale de Sangalkam a conduit à l’arrestation de dix individus de différentes nationalités. Parmi les personnes interpellées figurent sept ressortissants guinéens, deux Ivoiriennes et une Burkinabè. Cette intervention fait suite à des informations faisant état de l’existence présumée d’un réseau QNET dans la localité de Kounoune Centrale. Après leur interpellation, les dix suspects ont été conduits dans les locaux de l’unité de gendarmerie pour les besoins de l’enquête. Les investigations se poursuivent afin de faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire, notamment en déterminant l’ampleur des activités du réseau présumé et le degré d’implication de chacun des mis en cause. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Dix suspects interpellés dans une affaire présumée de réseau QNET est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: IR : trois tranches et un taux plafonné à 30 % d’ici 2031
items.description: Seuil d’exonération porté à 60 000 DH par an, barème ramené de cinq à trois tranches, taux marginal abaissé de 37 à 30 % : le programme gouvernemental 2026-2031 détaille sa réforme de l’impôt sur le revenu, qui sera déployée progressivement entre 2027 et 2031. Dans un contexte de hausse continue du coût de la vie, le programme gouvernemental 2026-2031 fait de l’impôt sur le revenu (IR) l’un des leviers de la restauration du pouvoir d’achat. La réforme figure à la page 58, au premier axe, intitulé « Restauration du pouvoir d’achat », de l’Axe 4 du document, consacré à ce même pouvoir d’achat et à la consolidation de l’État social. Elle se veut progressive et poursuit trois objectifs : alléger la charge fiscale pesant sur les salariés et la classe moyenne, simplifier le barème et encourager l’emploi déclaré. La première mesure concerne le seuil d’exonération. Le programme prévoit de relever la première tranche, celle du revenu net exonéré d’impôt, de 40 000 à 60 000 DH par an, soit un relèvement de 20 000 DH du plafond annuel exonéré. Concrètement, les salariés dont le revenu net n’excède pas 5 000 DH par mois ne seraient plus imposés. Le barème lui-même change de forme. Le nombre de tranches d’imposition passerait de cinq à trois, assorties de taux progressifs de 10 %, 20 % et 30 %. Cette refonte vise à rendre l’impôt plus lisible pour les contribuables, en remplaçant une structure jugée complexe par une grille resserrée. La réforme touche également le sommet du barème. Le taux marginal appliqué à la dernière tranche, celle des revenus les plus élevés, serait ramené de 37 à 30 %, soit une baisse de sept points. Associé au relèvement du seuil d’exonération, cet allègement doit réduire la pression fiscale sur les salariés et la classe moyenne, comme l’affiche l’objectif principal de la réforme. Ce dispositif se distingue de ce que proposait le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) durant la campagne des législatives. Dans son programme électoral, dévoilé le 1er septembre à Rabat, le parti proposait de ramener le barème de six à trois tranches et d’abaisser le taux marginal maximal de 37 à 20 %, soit dix points de moins que le taux de 30 % retenu par le Programme gouvernemental. Le texte prévoyait un taux nul pour les salaires bruts inférieurs à 15 000 DH, de 10 % entre 15 000 et 46 000 DH, puis de 20 % au-delà. L’exonération visait ainsi les rémunérations brutes allant jusqu’à 15 000 DH, soit environ 12 500 DH nets. À titre de comparaison, le programme gouvernemental retient une exonération de 60 000 DH nets par an, soit 5 000 DH par mois, et un taux marginal de 30 %. La promesse électorale avait d’ailleurs suscité des interrogations sur son financement, son coût pour les finances publiques pouvant se chiffrer en dizaines de milliards de dirhams. Le programme gouvernemental s’attache précisément à cet équilibre budgétaire. La réforme de l’IR sera déployée progressivement sur cinq ans, de 2027 à 2031, après évaluation de son coût financier et de ses impacts sur les revenus des ménages comme sur les recettes publiques. The post IR : trois tranches et un taux plafonné à 30 % d’ici 2031 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: Police warn politicians against inflammatory speeches during campaigns
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor The Commissioner of Police in Rivers State, Olugbenga Adepoju, has tasked political parties and their candidates for the 2027 elections to engage in issue-based campaigns and shun inflammatory rhetoric. This was as stakeholders, including party leaders, traditional rulers and civil society organisations, have called on political actors. security agencies and citizens to embrace peaceful conduct before, during and after the 2027 general elections. These calls formed the major discussions of the one-day Rivers Dialogue, organised by the newsroom of Megalectrics Limited, operators of Beat FM, Classic FM and Naija FM, in collaboration with the Professor Oke Onuchuku Institute of Peace and Conflict Studies, Ignatius Ajuru University of Education, Port Harcourt. The dialogue, themed “Peaceful Elections: Sustainable Path for Economic Development,” brought together political actors, traditional rulers and other stakeholders to discuss ways to prevent electoral violence and strengthen democracy in the 2027 polls. Addressing the participants, Adepoju said peaceful elections were necessary to sustain investors’ confidence, protect businesses and create an environment for development. Adepoju, who was represented by the Assistant Commissioner of Police (Operations) for the Rivers State Police Command, Ikechukwu Okoro, urged political parties to discourage violence among their supporters and advised candidates to focus on issue-based campaigns rather than inflammatory rhetoric. He further called on the media to use their platforms responsibly to promote peace rather than escalate tensions during the election. Meanwhile, Head of News Department, Megaletrics, Allwell Ene, said the dialogue was put together to ensure a violence free election in the state. He said: “The Rivers Dialogue was designed towards fostering violence-free and peaceful elections in Rivers State come 2027. Elections are critical periods in Nigeria because they alter the power structure within a state, the sub-national and the national levels where known political actors seek to establish their claims to power.” Ene noted that the state is notorious for electoral violence and security breaches during elections in the country, adding that such violence spills into other elections which subsequently paralyses governance and economic activities in the state; hence, the dialogue intends to address some of the issues. Also speaking, the Director-General of the National Orientation Agency, Mallam Lanre Issa-Onilu, said credible elections required the collective responsibility of citizens, political institutions and electoral stakeholders. Issa-Onilu, represented by the Rivers State Director of NOA, Dr Banigo Edward, said the increasing number of registered voters alone could not guarantee credible elections without civic discipline, active participation and responsible conduct before, during and after the polls. He said: “A free, fair and credible election in 2027 cannot be guaranteed by INEC alone. It requires a collective responsibility, civic discipline, moral courage and active participation of every citizen.” However, the Paramount Ruler of Elelenwo Etor Kingdom in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of the state, His Royal Highness, Eze Sunny Weli Chukwu, called for proper training and orientation for security personnel deployed for election monitoring to prevent unnecessary violence. Chukwu urged the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure eligible voters had access to their Permanent Voter Cards and called on traditional rulers to educate their communities, particularly youths, against electoral violence and vote-buying. Meanwhile, the All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Rivers State, Hon. Kingsley Ogundu Chinda, pledged his commitment to peaceful elections and governance, emphasising that protecting lives and property remained the primary responsibility of government. He said, “I am fully, unconditionally committed to a peaceful election and peaceful governance in Rivers State.” Other governorship candidates, including those of the Social Democratic Party and the Peoples Redemption Party, National Rescue Movement as well as Boot, also expressed their commitment to non-violent elections in the state. The post 2027: Police warn politicians against inflammatory speeches during campaigns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: This Is Not a Cycle of Retribution
items.description: Donald Trump has spent nearly two years investigating, suing, or prosecuting anybody in politics, media, or government who ever defied him. Now, with Democrats poised to win control of one or both chambers of Congress, the administration and its allies are prepared to slip back into their familiar pose of victimhood. The putative evidence of imminent GOP persecution comes from Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who recently told the Vox journalist Astead Herndon during an event at the University of Chicago that Democrats should pursue accountability for the administration to, among other goals, deter new graduates from enlisting in corrupt schemes. “I want young people coming out of school to say, ‘Should I go work for the Trump administration?’” she said. “I want them to be like, ‘Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don’t want, and so let me avoid participating in that.’” Slotkin made these remarks last Tuesday, attracting little notice at the time because she didn’t say anything particularly noteworthy. Five days later, a tidal wave of conservative outrage suddenly crashed over her. The Republican response has been revealing. Even Trump-skeptical conservatives are signaling that, just as they have in the past, his party will rally behind him the moment someone proposes that the laws of the country should be enforced if Trump is found to have engaged in misconduct. He has trained members of his party to sublimate any concern they may have about his actions beneath their partisan instincts. However queasy Trump might occasionally make them, they will return to his side the moment he faces the prospect of legal consequences. [ From the October 2026 issue: MAGA is making the world safe for corruption ] “It is absolutely disgraceful to threaten young Americans for participating in politics and serving their country,” Senator Mike Lee, a Utah Republican, complained . “This type of thinking is terrible for our country,” Ari Fleischer, the former press secretary to President George W. Bush, chimed in . Columns by the Trump legal adviser Mike Davis in Fox News and the writer Miranda Devine in the New York Post depict Slotkin as a goon who was menacing bright-eyed youth for no reason other than their partisan affiliation. “Slotkin is a lowlife who’s ruining her state,” Trump said in front of the White House when prodded for a reaction by a reporter. Trump went even further, as is his wont. “That’s a hell of a statement,” he told reporters. “Slotkin said that there should be prosecutions in order to scare people from going into politics.” In point of fact, Slotkin didn’t say anything about prosecutions. She was discussing congressional oversight and specifically describing a scenario in which Democrats had control of Congress but not the executive branch. She was arguing for a measured and focused approach, prioritizing only the most blatant forms of corruption. “We do have to have accountability for the unbelievable corruption that we are living under right now,” she said. “But you can’t just make that your whole personality. So you have to pick signature cases, and you have to go after people and projects that are just super egregious.” Later in the conversation, Herndon noted that Trump has largely insulated himself from accountability by stacking the courts and installing loyalists throughout his party and the federal government. That’s when Slotkin pointed out that exposing the administration’s corruption might deter ambitious Republicans from joining the administration during its final years. The outraged responses omitted the first part of Slotkin’s remarks, which point out the need to investigate the administration’s pervasive misconduct. Out of context, it sounds as if Slotkin is threatening young Republicans because of malevolence. But in context, her comments are understandable, even generous. If you knew a young person who had been planning to go to work for Elizabeth Holmes, deterring them by exposing the Theranos founder as a con artist would have been doing them a favor. Pretending that the Trump administration is innocent is just the first line of defense. The fallback argument against investigating, and perhaps eventually prosecuting, any corruption is that doing so will set off a cycle of retribution. A Wall Street Journal editorial accuses Slotkin of “essentially promising a scorched-earth lawfare campaign” that will invite reprisals. “This is where the multiple prosecutions that Democrats unleashed against Mr. Trump in the Biden years are taking us. Mr. Trump is retaliating with similar attempts to criminalize political differences. And now Ms. Slotkin is vowing more of the same. Down this road lies more bitterness and political dysfunction,” the Journal editorial laments. Jack Goldsmith, a former Bush-administration legal adviser, makes a similar argument in a Substack column . The fear that the two parties are locked in a cycle of retribution has a certain high-minded but superficial appeal. It’s true that Trump faced investigations after leaving office, and that he has cited these investigations as a rationale for his reign of legal terror. But Joe Biden did not behave in a remotely similar fashion. He appointed an attorney general, Merrick Garland, who commanded bipartisan respect. Garland operated cautiously, following traditional procedure, and appointed Jack Smith as a special counsel when evidence of Trump’s refusal to cooperate with the investigation—taking classified documents, stonewalling repeated requests to return them, and then trying to mislead federal investigators—was too blatant to ignore. Trump did face one questionable prosecution: Alvin Bragg, the Manhattan prosecutor, charged that his hush money to Stormy Daniels was a campaign-finance violation. But that was not something Biden directed. Besides, Trump’s ambition to imprison his opponents preceded anything Biden did, as anybody who remembers the “Lock her up!” chants should readily concede. Trump was unable to effectively prosecute his enemies during his first term, largely because he was stuck with a Justice Department whose staff was committed to traditional norms of independence, not for lack of trying. To the contrary, Trump spent most of his first term trying to make his attorneys general act like Roy Cohn. He pressured Ukraine’s government to gin up an investigation of Biden, and he eventually appointed a special counsel, John Durham, to investigate various enemies, only for Durham to fall on his face. [ Leo J. Wise: How corruption got this bad ] The most logical way to understand Trump’s motive is that he has always viewed laws as suggestions rather than hard requirements, and tended to assume that people in power will abuse it to protect their friends and punish their enemies. Democratic lawfare did not implant this belief in Trump. He and his allies are going to continue investigating fake crimes and committing real ones, because Trump fundamentally does not believe in the rule of law. What is most peculiar is that the Democrats aren’t the party that has decided to elevate this question in the closing days of the midterm campaign. The Republicans are. Why, you might wonder, did a phalanx of Republicans emerge several days after the fact to start screaming about Slotkin? Anti-anti-Trump Republicans, of which the Journal is a leading voice, often invoke the Mueller investigation and the first Trump impeachment as radicalizing events that reignited their wavering partisan attachment. The misguided Bragg indictment of Trump helped rehabilitate him among Republicans who had been ready to move on after January 6. As Davis wrote on X, “Dear @ElissaSlotkin : You are rallying fractured Republicans right before the midterms.” Trump in his second term has operated with complete impunity. The Republican Congress is not even pretending to conduct oversight over the executive branch, and the Justice Department is not even pretending to care whether the president and his allies follow the law. The president grasps that if he ever has to face accountability, his party will back him up. Trump has two modes: flaunting his impunity and wallowing in victimization. For the moment, he finds the latter more politically useful.

items.title: YEA to deploy 6,000 community teaching assistants by November – Basintale
items.description: The Youth Employment Agency (YEA) plans to onboard and deploy 6,000 community teaching assistants by the end of November 2026 under an agreement with the Ghana Education Service (GES). Chief Executive Officer Malik Basintale announced the plan when he addressed the Government Accountability Series at the Jubilee House on Wednesday, October 21. He said the Agency signed a memorandum of understanding with the GES in September to facilitate the recruitment and deployment of the beneficiaries, who are expected to support basic schools, particularly in hard-to-reach communities. The initiative is designed to provide additional teaching support where needed while giving qualified young people practical classroom experience and an opportunity to develop their professional skills. “In this regard, I am happy to report that as recently as September this year, the YEA had signed a successful Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ghana Education Service for the onboarding of some 6000 beneficiaries, who will be deployed by the end of November this year,” Mr Basintale said. The programme is among the Agency’s interventions aimed at combining employment creation with support for essential public services. Mr Basintale said the YEA’s broader mandate was to work with other institutions to provide training, workplace attachment and skills development rather than directly employ beneficiaries into mainstream public and private sector positions.

items.title: Uganda denies Ebola outbreak after Nigeria confirms imported case
items.description: Uganda has denied having an active Ebola outbreak following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), insisting that it has no confirmed active infections as authorities investigate where the patient contracted the virus. In a public statement issued in Kampala on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Uganda’s Ministry of Health said the Nigerian patient had travelled through the country before arriving in Nigeria but stressed that her transit did not establish where she was infected. “We wish to clarify that, as at the time of this statement, Uganda has NO confirmed active Ebola cases,” the ministry said. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: We Call for Calm and Vigilance,” added that preliminary information indicated the woman had travelled through Uganda in early October without symptoms and developed them after arriving in Nigeria. “Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said. It added that Nigeria’s government was expected to provide detailed information about the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to support further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The Ugandan authorities also said they were strengthening screening and public health controls at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, announced the confirmed case on Tuesday, saying laboratory tests had established that the woman was infected with Ebola virus disease. According to Pate, the patient had recently travelled to East Africa, including Uganda, before returning to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7. Her condition reportedly worsened four days later, prompting further medical attention and testing. The woman was admitted to a private hospital, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She has since been isolated and is receiving medical care. Pate said health authorities had identified 44 contacts and commenced contact tracing to prevent further transmission. Surveillance has also been strengthened at Nigeria’s points of entry. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare is coordinating the response with the FCT Health Services Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and other public health partners. The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities to remain vigilant and maintain a high index of suspicion for possible Ebola cases, particularly among patients with relevant travel histories and compatible symptoms. He also urged Nigerians to remain calm, practise good hygiene and promptly seek medical attention if they experience symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. Uganda recorded Ebola infections earlier in 2026 but subsequently declared the outbreak over after meeting the required conditions for ending transmission. In its latest statement, the Ugandan Ministry of Health urged the public to remain calm and vigilant, practise regular handwashing and sanitisation, and follow verified updates from official channels. items.title: Un premier cas d’Ebola confirmé à Abuja
items.description: Le Nigeria a annoncé, mardi 20 octobre 2026, la confirmation d’un premier cas d’infection au virus Ebola sur son territoire. La patiente, récemment arrivée d’Ouganda, est prise en charge en isolement dans la capitale, Abuja. Les autorités sanitaires ont lancé le traçage des contacts, tandis que plusieurs pays africains restent confrontés à la circulation du virus. Le Nigeria fait face à son premier cas confirmé d’Ebola. L’information a été annoncée, le mardi 20 octobre 2026 par le ministre de la Santé, Muhammad Ali Pate, après la confirmation de l’infection par des analyses de laboratoire. Selon les informations communiquées par le ministre, la patiente est une femme récemment arrivée d’Ouganda à bord d’un vol international. Elle avait été admise dans un établissement hospitalier privé d’Abuja, où elle a reçu des soins pendant plusieurs jours avant que le diagnostic ne soit établi. Elle est actuellement placée en isolement et bénéficie d’une prise en charge médicale. Face à cette situation, le gouvernement a appelé les structures sanitaires publiques et privées du pays à renforcer leur vigilance et à se mettre en état d’alerte maximale. Cette nouvelle intervient dans un contexte de recrudescence de la maladie sur le continent africain. Depuis mai 2026, la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) est confrontée à la 17ᵉ épidémie d’Ebola de son histoire. D’après les derniers chiffres publiés lundi 19 octobre par les autorités sanitaires congolaises, cette flambée a déjà enregistré 9 455 cas confirmés et 4 561 décès, ce qui en fait la plus meurtrière jamais connue dans le pays. Le Kenya est également concerné par cette dynamique épidémique. Mardi 20 octobre, le pays a signalé un neuvième cas lié à l’épidémie en cours, alors qu’un décès y a déjà été enregistré. La confirmation du cas nigérian vient ainsi renforcer les préoccupations liées à la propagation transfrontalière du virus Ebola en Afrique. Le suivi rigoureux des contacts, le dépistage précoce et l’isolement rapide des personnes infectées demeurent des mesures essentielles pour limiter les risques de transmission et contenir l’épidémie. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un premier cas d’Ebola confirmé à Abuja est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Black Bombers arrive in Kinshasa for 2026 IBA Africa Elite Boxing Championships
items.description: Ghana’s Black Bombers have arrived in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, ahead of the 2026 IBA Africa Elite Men’s and Women’s Boxing Championships. The competition, scheduled to run from October 19 to November 1, will provide the national team with an opportunity to test its readiness against some of the continent’s best boxers. Ghana will be represented by Amadu Mohammed in the bantamweight division (55kg), Ebenezer Ankrah in the lightweight category (60kg) and Joseph “Jaguar” Commey in the light welterweight division (63.5kg). Second lead coach Charles Quartey will head Ghana’s technical team for the championship as the boxers seek to make an impact in Kinshasa. The tournament forms part of Ghana’s preparations for the 2028 Olympic boxing qualifiers, with the Black Bombers targeting strong performances as they build towards the qualifying campaign. Ghana hopes to use the competition to assess its boxers, gain valuable international experience and strengthen its medal prospects ahead of the Olympic qualification process. The team’s participation aligns with its broader ambition to secure multiple medals at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. The championships will bring together elite male and female boxers from across Africa, offering the Ghanaian contingent an important test against continental opposition.

items.title: Élections israéliennes : Netanyahou utilise les violences en France pour renforcer son discours sécuritaire
items.description: Le Premier ministre israelien Benjamin Netanyahou relie directement les recentes violences en France aux consequences du 7-Octobre. Dans un entretien accorde le 20 octobre a i24NEWS, il affirme avoir averti le president francais Emmanuel Macron des 2023 : « Si nous ne les eliminons pas ici, vous les aurez a Paris. » Il ajoute desormais : « Et c'est exactement ce qui se passe. » Netanyahou raconte que Macron l'avait appele apres l'attaque du 7-Octobre pour evoquer une solution diplomatique. Il dit lui avoir repondu que le Hamas devait etre combattu comme l'organisation etat islamique et qu'une strategie d'« apaisement » ne ferait que deplacer la menace vers l'Europe. Interroge sur les troubles en France, il accuse les autorites de ne pas s'etre preparees et d'avoir « cede a l'invasion de l'islam extremiste ». Son conseil a la France est tout aussi direct : : « Battez-vous, ne jouez pas l'apaisement, battez-vous contre les extremistes ». Une comparaison contestee La comparaison est neanmoins tres contestable sur le plan factuel. Les manifestations francaises sont nees de revendications portant notamment sur le coût de la vie et les services publics avant de degenerer, dans plusieurs villes, en pillages et affrontements. Les autorites mettent en cause des groupes d'ultragauche et des casseurs opportunistes. Le rapprochement opere par Netanyahou ne repose sur aucun element tangible. Ces propos surviennent a quelques jours des elections israeliennes du 27 octobre. Netanyahou mene campagne sur la securite, l'Iran et la necessite de maintenir une ligne militaire dure. En invoquant la France, il cherche aussi a presenter le combat mene par Israel depuis le 7 octobre comme une bataille depassant ses propres frontieres et concernant directement l'Europe. La logique israelienne consiste ainsi a montrer que l'etat hebreu est le dernier rempart face a l'islamisme avant qu'il ne deferle sur l'Europe, une ideologie qui s'appuie sur la theorie du « choc des civilisations » du politologue americain Samuel P. Huntington.

items.title: NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI) has unveiled an investment and development-finance pipeline exceeding $600 million for solar energy and other development initiatives, following the participation of 298 Nigerian innovators at the NextGen Innovation Challenge 2026 in London. The proposed financing comprises a $500 million solar-energy programme for universities and polytechnics and a $100 million financing arrangement for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The funds, however, have not been confirmed as received or fully mobilised. Speaking at a world press conference on Wednesday, NBTI Director-General, Dr Kazeem Kolawole Raji, said the October 9 event, organised in partnership with UKALD, provided an international platform for showcasing Nigerian technologies and connecting innovators with investors and commercial partners. The number of participating innovators rose from 105 in 2025 to 298 this year, representing all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with innovations spanning agriculture, healthcare, artificial intelligence, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing. “Our innovators have demonstrated that Nigeria has ideas worthy of international attention. Our responsibility is to help create the conditions in which those ideas can grow, compete and deliver lasting value to our people,” Raji said. NBTI said discussions with Gigawatt Global focused on developing solar farms in universities and polytechnics under power purchase agreements, while a memorandum of understanding with Financial Innovation for Impact, UK, also known as Cambridge Investors, covered the proposed $100 million financing for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The initiative targets one million micro and small businesses for solar-energy solutions, 50,000 direct youth jobs and 10,000 trained field marketers, with ₦30 billion in blended financing targeted for its first phase. Other outcomes include an announced $100,000 investment commitment by Dubai-based investor Erin Grover for three women innovators and international acceleration opportunities valued at $160,000 for 16 selected innovators. The Learning and Development Bureau UK also offered leadership and management scholarships worth more than £80,000 collectively to the 16 innovators and pledged assistance with UK Global Talent Visa applications, subject to eligibility. Raji said the priority was now to turn the opportunities into viable businesses, jobs and measurable economic benefits, urging investors and development partners to support Nigerian innovators with funding, mentorship and market access. “Our focus must now move decisively from visibility to implementation, from promising concepts to commercially viable solutions, and from announcements to independently verifiable outcomes,” he said. The post NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Who protects the dreamer? (Part II) — Reflections on the vulnerability of the Girl Child in the Obuasi Senior High Technical School Scandal
items.description: By Thelma Takyiwaa Ankomah There is something sickeningly cruel about a society that encourages a girl to dream, sends her to school to build that dream, and then leaves her vulnerable to the very people entrusted with protecting her. The allegations emerging from Obuasi Senior High Technical School against its headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, involving sexual abuse, including rape, are deeply disturbing. If established, these allegations would represent not merely a crime, but a monstrous betrayal of trust, authority and the sacred responsibility of educating children. I am angry. Deeply angry. And every Ghanaian who cares about the safety of our children should be furious. What makes this matter particularly horrifying is the power imbalance between a school authority and the students placed under his care. A school should be a sanctuary of learning, not a place where a girl must fear the person who ought to protect her. I strongly encourage everyone to watch “ Inside the dreaded headmaster’s bungalow” By Manasseh Azure Awuni – JoyNews on this scandal. Watch it with an open mind, but prepare yourself emotionally. The revelations are deeply disturbing, and you may find yourself asking how such allegations could emerge from an institution entrusted with the future of young people. You will be angry. You will be troubled. And you will understand why silence, indifference and institutional complacency are unacceptable. When the protector becomes the subject of allegations A headmaster is entrusted with authority, not given a licence to intimidate, exploit or abuse. That position exists to protect students, not expose them to danger. We must ask the hard questions. Were complaints previously made? Who received them? Who acted, and who looked away? Were warning signs ignored? Did anyone use influence, position or political connections to suppress concerns? If institutional failures occurred, those responsible must be identified and held accountable. Ghana cannot afford another theatrical investigation in which committees are established, press statements are issued, and eventually everybody returns to business as usual. Enough of the hypocrisy. Enough of the institutional cowardice. Enough of treating the suffering of vulnerable children as a public-relations inconvenience. Where is the ministry responsible for protecting our girls? The Ghana Education Service, the Ghana Police Service, the Attorney-General’s Department and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection must demonstrate urgency, competence and moral courage. Madam Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, protecting children cannot be a ministerial title displayed on an official website. It must be demonstrated when girls are allegedly violated and the nation demands answers. Where is the visible, forceful advocacy for these girls? Where is the unmistakable demand for their protection, counselling, dignity and justice? This is not the time for timid statements or bureaucratic excuses. It is time to stand firmly with vulnerable children and insist that every relevant institution does its job. No political shields. No selective justice. The NDC’s statement of 20th October 2026 calling for Mr Abdulai to step aside to facilitate an unhindered investigation was welcome. But the circumstances surrounding the matter also demand scrutiny of how concerns were handled. Political affiliation must never become a protective shield. Neither should public outrage become a substitute for evidence. The presumption of innocence must be respected, but due process must not be weaponised to justify inaction. Who protects the dreamer? Red Wednesday must become more than wearing red for photographs and social media attention. It must become a national revolt against the normalisation of abuse, the protection of powerful individuals and the abandonment of vulnerable girls. If the allegations are proven, justice must be uncompromising. If officials failed in their duties, they must answer. If institutional weaknesses enabled abuse, they must be exposed and corrected. Our girls are not bargaining chips. Their dignity is not negotiable. Their futures must never be sacrificed to protect powerful people, political parties or institutional reputations. No cover-ups. No excuses. No selective accountability. No investigation as usual. Justice for our girls. Protect the dreamer. No cover-ups. No selective accountability. No investigation as usual. Justice for our girls, without fear or favour. #RedWednesday #ProtectTheGirlChild #JusticeForOurGirls #InstitutionalAccountability #NoOneIsAbovmeTheLaw

items.title: Obuasi SHTS students remain at home nearly 3 months after closure over headmaster’s sexual abuse claims
items.description: The academic future of many second-year and final-year students of Obuasi Senior High and Technical School (SHTS) remains uncertain, as the school has been closed to continuing students for nearly three months. The school was shut down on August 5 following an order by the municipal assembly after a riot in which students reportedly attacked the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. Despite the commencement of the new academic year for senior high schools, academic activities at Obuasi SHTS have yet to resume for continuing students. JoyNews checks in the mining town revealed that some second-year and final-year students were helping with domestic chores, while others were engaged in trading activities, with no clear indication of when they would return to the classroom. Anthony Coffie, president of a group known as Concerned Citizens of Adansi, has expressed concern over the situation and called for the students to be allowed to return to school. “The situation is particularly alarming for Form Three students, who should be preparing intensively for their West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE). The loss of valuable instructional time threatens their examination preparation and academic prospects,” he said. Mr Coffie said students should not be made to suffer the consequences of what he described as an administrative crisis, stressing the need to protect their right to education. “Our children must not become collateral victims of an administrative crisis. Their right to education and their prospects for academic success must not be sacrificed while the relevant authorities deliberate over the issues surrounding the school,” he said. He is appealing to the Adansihene to engage the government, the Minister for Education and the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES) to put immediate and effective measures in place to reopen the school. He also called for appropriate safety arrangements to protect students when academic activities resume.

items.title: PANDEF mourns Uduaghan, hails his peacebuilding role
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, who died three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, described Uduaghan as an exceptional leader whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unwavering. Igali stated this in a condolence letter to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on the death of the former governor, according to a statement issued on Wednesday. He praised Uduaghan for his significant contributions to peace and stability in the Niger Delta, particularly during his tenure as Secretary to the State Government and later as governor, when militancy was heightened across the region. In the letter, Igali said he was shocked by the news of Uduaghan’s death, describing the late governor as a close associate and personal friend. “I write to express my total shock at the news of the passing into glory of our dearly beloved brother, the former Governor of Delta State, HE Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan. Although we mourn, but we all hold strong belief that the Almighty God knows best, and we glorify His exalted name,” he said. Igali added that he and Uduaghan had maintained a cordial relationship since they served simultaneously as secretaries to their respective state governments. “Without doubt, he was an exceptional man through and through, whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unfettered,” he said. He noted that Uduaghan played a significant role in bringing peace and stability to the Niger Delta during a period of heightened militancy in the South-South region. Igali described the former governor’s death as a major loss not only to Delta State but also to the Niger Delta and Nigeria as a whole. He expressed hope that Uduaghan’s legacy of service to God and humanity would endure, saying the late governor had “embedded his name in gold in the annals of our history.” Igali also asked Oborevwori to convey his deepest condolences to the Uduaghan family and the people of Delta State, praying for the repose of the former governor’s soul. items.title: Showunmi reaffirms commitment to Abiola’s legacy, national unity
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of the Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi has reaffirmed his commitment to Nigeria’s unity, democratic development and the ideals for which the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale (MKO) Abiola sacrificed his life, insisting that the struggle to actualise the June 12, 1993 presidential election mandate remains a defining moment in his political journey. Showunmi, in a statement titled “My Scar from MKO Abiola, My Sacrifice for Democracy, and My Unwavering Pan-Nigerian Conviction,” said the circumstances surrounding Abiola’s death and the annulment of the historic election had left an indelible mark on his life and political convictions. He also cautioned political actors against actions capable of undermining national stability, particularly the premature or unauthorised announcement of election results in ways that could trigger political tension and plunge the country into chaos. “The scar in my heart from the loss of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola has not fully healed,” Showunmi said, adding that he would neither trivialise Abiola’s sacrifice nor pretend to be unfamiliar with the painful experiences that shaped Nigeria’s democratic struggle. He stressed that his remarks on the country’s political history had been misunderstood by some people, insisting that his intention was to caution against political conduct that could endanger peace, violate the law or destabilise the nation. Showunmi said his reference to the political events of 1992 was intended to illustrate the consequences of abandoning caution, restraint and respect for the law in the pursuit of political power. “I invoked the events of 1992 to illustrate how political situations can spiral out of control when caution, restraint and respect for the law are abandoned,” he said. He maintained that his intervention was intended as a warning about the potential consequences of political decisions, not an endorsement of reckless conduct. “My intervention was a warning about consequences, not an invitation to recklessness, and I will not permit reactionary forces to turn my counsel into something it was never intended to be,” he stated. According to him, political advice should be offered in the national interest, while individuals must ultimately decide whether to heed such counsel. He urged political contestants to consider the wider implications of their actions, warning that decisions taken without regard for the law and national stability could have far-reaching consequences for the country. Reaffirming his commitment to national unity, Showunmi declared that his political convictions were not driven by ethnic considerations and rejected any suggestion that he subscribed to the superiority of one ethnic group over another. “I must also state, unequivocally, that I am a Pan-Nigerian through and through. I have no interest in promoting the idea that one ethnic group is superior to another,” he said. He explained that his political philosophy was rooted in the collective dignity, security and prosperity of Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic or regional backgrounds. Showunmi urged Yoruba activists and others who might disagree with his position to consider his statements within the broader context of his commitment to Nigeria’s unity. “My words and actions must be understood within the framework of my commitment to the Nigerian nation. I will not subordinate that commitment to ethnic sentiment, sectional advantage or the politics of exclusion,” he said. He added that his preference for national cohesion should not be interpreted as a lack of personal conviction or an inadequate understanding of the country’s political history. On Nigeria’s political future, Showunmi reiterated his support for a power-sharing arrangement under which the presidency would rotate between the northern and southern parts of the country. He argued that a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation could help reduce political suspicion, strengthen national cohesion and promote democratic stability. “I have long expressed the view that Nigeria should manage political power through a pendulum arrangement between the Northern and Southern parts of the country,” he said. “In my considered opinion, a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation offers a framework for reducing suspicion, strengthening national cohesion and sustaining our democratic journey.” He described the proposal as part of the broader need for political maturity, mutual understanding and an inclusive approach to managing Nigeria’s diversity. Paying tribute to Abiola, the presumed winner of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, which was annulled by the military government, Showunmi said the late politician’s legacy remained inseparable from Nigeria’s struggle for democratic governance. He prayed that Abiola’s sacrifice would continue to inspire Nigerians to work towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. “May your supreme sacrifice continue to guide Nigeria towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. May the promise for which you paid such a terrible price never be betrayed,” he said. Showunmi also disclosed that he intended to speak more extensively in the future about his personal contributions to the pro-democracy struggle and how the events surrounding Abiola shaped his political trajectory. “One day, God willing, I will speak more fully about my own contributions to the struggle for democracy,” he said. According to him, the experiences surrounding Abiola and the struggle to reclaim the June 12 mandate influenced his political outlook and redirected the course of his life, setting in motion developments whose consequences he said were still unfolding. He also acknowledged the role played by media entrepreneur and publisher Dele Momodu during that period, describing his contribution as significant to that chapter of Nigeria’s political history. “I must also acknowledge Dele Momodu. May God spare his life. He played a key and pivotal role in that chapter of our history, and his contribution deserves to be remembered,” Showunmi said. Showunmi warned against interpreting his restraint as a lack of knowledge of Nigeria’s democratic history or mistaking his commitment to national unity for an absence of personal convictions. “Finally, let nobody mistake my restraint for ignorance of history or my commitment to national unity for an absence of personal conviction,” he said. He added: “My commitment is to Nigeria. My loyalty is to the democratic ideal. My respect for MKO Abiola’s sacrifice is enduring. And my conviction that Nigeria must survive, mature and prosper remains unshaken.” “May God bless Nigeria and all who genuinely labour for her progress,” he said. The post Showunmi reaffirms commitment to Abiola’s legacy, national unity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ferme géante Baladna d’Adrar : les trois objectifs majeurs de l’Algérie
items.description: La facture des importations réduite de 1,5 milliard de dollars par un seul projet : l’Algérie est en train de transformer le désert du Sahara en pôle agricole d'excellence et en pilier de sa souveraineté alimentaire. Les promesses de la ferme géante Baladna Algérie , implantée à Adrar, sont à la mesure de son gigantisme. Avec ce projet hors normes, l’Algérie poursuit trois objectifs majeurs : renforcer sa souveraineté alimentaire et faire du Sahara un pôle d’excellence agricole. Baladna Algérie : une production de 1,7 milliards de litres de lait à partir de fin 2027 Le projet intégré a reçu lundi 19 octobre la visite du ministre de l’Agriculture Sid Ali Khaldi qui a constaté sur place le taux satisfaisant de l’avancement des travaux : 80%. A ce rythme, la production de lait cru débutera à la fin de l’année 2027 et celle de lait en poudre début 2028. Le projet, fruit d’un investissement algéro-qatarie de 3,5 milliards de dollars, intègre la culture de fourrages à grande échelle, un élevage bovin de 240 000 vaches et une usine de production de poudre de lait. La capacité de production prévue est de 1,7 milliards de lait cru qui serviront à la production de 193 000 tonnes de poudre de lait par an, avec l'ambition stratégique de couvrir, à terme, 50 % des besoins nationaux de poudre de lait. Baladna Algérie : les premières génisses attendues fin novembre des États-Unis La superficie totale dédiée au projet est de 219 000 hectares. Le projet a également une dimension sociale avec la prévision de la création d’un total de 20 000 emplois. L’introduction des premières génisses, au nombre de 35 000, débutera fin novembre prochain. Elles seront importées des États-Unis. Les travaux vont bon train, a constaté le ministre, accompagné du wali d'Adrar et du président du conseil d'administration de Baladna El Djazaïr, Ali Al Ali. Au total, 102 lots ont été attribués, dont 69 % à des entreprises algériennes. Le projet mobilise actuellement 1 360 travailleurs. “Faire du Sud algérien un pôle d'excellence de l'investissement agricole” La ferme géante Baladna Algérie dynamisera aussi l'économie saharienne en développant la production locale de viande rouge et en favorisant un transfert technologique majeur pour l'agriculture nationale, indique l’entreprise. “Nous avons pour ambition de faire du Sud algérien un pôle d'excellence de l'investissement agricole, capable de valoriser les potentialités de la région et de soutenir le développement de filières agricoles intégrées”, a déclaré sur place le ministre Sid Ali Khaldi. “Ce que bâtit Baladna El Djazaïr aujourd'hui à Adrar constitue le socle de la sécurité alimentaire, en matière de lait, de toute l'Algérie pour les années à venir, où son engagement quotidien se résume en une promesse : Building today, feeding tomorrow (construire aujourd’hui, nourrir demain)”, a assuré pour sa part Ali Al Ali. L’article Ferme géante Baladna d’Adrar : les trois objectifs majeurs de l’Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Tras la decisión del Constitucional sobre la ‘ley de nietos’ ¿Sigue suspendido el voto? ¿Podrán participar el 29-N?
items.description: El Tribunal Constitucional ha rechazado intervenir en el debate jurídico que se mantiene en el Tribunal Supremo sobre el derecho al voto de 163.000 nacionalizados por la ya conocida como ley de nietos que viven en el extranjero. Los magistrados han desestimado la petición del Defensor del Pueblo de levantar la suspensión cautelar del sufragio de estos españoles de cara a las elecciones generales del 29-N. El tribunal de garantías ha adoptado esta decisión al considerar que el movimiento impulsado por la institución encabezada por Ángel Gabilondo era prematuro porque no se ha agotado todavía la vía abierta en el Supremo. items.title: Rusia libera al estadounidense Stephen Hubbard en pleno acercamiento entre Trump y Putin
items.description: El presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin , recibe este miércoles al enviado especial de Donald Trump, el empresario Steve Witkoff , con un preso estadounidense y unos barriles de diésel como ofrenda. El dirigente ha entregado a Washington al profesor de 74 años Stephen James Hubbard, capturado en Ucrania durante la invasión rusa, y ha anunciado que zarpará en los próximos días el primer carguero ruso con el combustible prometido a Trump de cara a sus elecciones. Unos gestos, la entrega de un rehén estadounidense y el diésel, que la Casa Blanca ha recibido con los brazos abiertos mientras busca hacer negocios con el Kremlin y un encuentro trilateral con el dirigente ruso y el presidente ucranio, Volodímir Zelenski, al que presiona para que capitule a las exigencias rusas. items.title: La Tunisienne Amal Mekni parmi les 100 femmes héroïnes de la FAO
items.description: À travers son exploitation agricole, son engagement pour la valorisation des produits locaux et son action auprès des femmes en milieu rural, Amal Mekni incarne une agriculture tunisienne innovante, inclusive et durable. Sa reconnaissance par la FAO met en lumière le rôle moteur des femmes dans la transformation des systèmes agroalimentaires. De la région de Béja au siège de la FAO à Rome, le parcours d’Amal Mekni illustre la capacité des femmes à transformer les défis du monde rural en opportunités économiques et sociales. Ingénieure agronome et entrepreneure agricole tunisienne, elle figure parmi les 100 femmes héroïnes des systèmes agroalimentaires et du développement rural distinguées par l’Organisation des Nations Unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO), dans le cadre de l’Année internationale des agricultrices 2026. La cérémonie de reconnaissance s’est tenue le 15 octobre au siège de la FAO, à Rome, en marge du Forum mondial de l’alimentation. Cette distinction internationale salue des femmes dont le leadership, l’expertise et l’innovation contribuent à renforcer les systèmes agroalimentaires, à créer des opportunités pour les communautés rurales et à promouvoir un développement plus durable et inclusif. La sélection a été effectuée à l’issue d’un processus international ayant reçu 609 candidatures provenant de 131 membres de la FAO . De l’expertise agronomique à l’entrepreneuriat agricole À la tête de La Reine du Nord , une exploitation agricole située dans le gouvernorat de Béja, Amal Mekni a choisi de mettre ses compétences au service du développement agricole de sa région. Après une expérience dans l’industrie agroalimentaire, elle s’est engagée dans l’entrepreneuriat, avec l’ambition de valoriser les ressources locales et de développer une activité créatrice de valeur. Son projet s’inscrit dans une logique de valorisation des produits du terroir, notamment à travers l’élevage et la transformation laitière. Cette orientation avait déjà été mise en lumière par la FAO en 2021, lorsqu’Amal Mekni figurait parmi les jeunes entrepreneures accompagnées dans le cadre d’un programme consacré à l’investissement responsable des jeunes dans l’agriculture . Son projet portait alors sur l’élevage de brebis de race locale Thibar et la production de fromages de qualité, avec une ambition affirmée de valoriser les produits typiques du nord de Béja. Au-delà de la production, cette démarche illustre l’intérêt de rapprocher savoir-faire agronomique, transformation agroalimentaire et valorisation commerciale des produits locaux. Elle témoigne également du potentiel de l’entrepreneuriat agricole pour stimuler l’économie régionale et contribuer à la création d’activités et d’emplois en milieu rural. Un engagement qui dépasse les frontières de son exploitation La portée du parcours d’Amal Mekni réside aussi dans son engagement en faveur des autres femmes en milieu rural. Celle-ci préside un groupement de développement agricole féminin et accompagne une trentaine de femmes vers une plus grande autonomie économique. Elle contribue également au développement des compétences, avec plus de 100 stagiaires formés, et soutient des initiatives génératrices de revenus. Cette dimension collective donne une portée particulière à son engagement, car au-delà de la réussite d’une entreprise, il s’agit de favoriser l’accès des femmes aux compétences, de soutenir leurs initiatives économiques et de renforcer leur participation à la création de valeur dans les territoires ruraux. En mettant l’accent sur la valorisation des productions locales et l’autonomie économique des femmes, son expérience illustre une approche du développement rural dans laquelle l’innovation et la performance agricole peuvent aller de pair avec l’inclusion sociale. Mettre les femmes en milieu rural au premier plan La distinction accordée à Amal Mekni par la FAO dépasse la reconnaissance d’un parcours individuel. Elle contribue à rendre plus visibles les compétences, l’expertise et le leadership des femmes qui participent quotidiennement au fonctionnement des systèmes agroalimentaires, souvent sans bénéficier d’une reconnaissance à la hauteur de leur contribution. Cette mise en lumière prend un relief particulier en 2026, proclamée Année internationale des agricultrices par les Nations Unies. L’initiative vise notamment à sensibiliser à la contribution essentielle des femmes à l’agriculture , à la sécurité alimentaire et à la résilience économique, tout en attirant l’attention sur les inégalités qui limitent encore leur accès aux ressources, aux services et aux opportunités.. Pour la Tunisie, le parcours d’Amal Mekni constitue un exemple inspirant de la manière dont l’entrepreneuriat agricole peut contribuer à dynamiser les territoires, à valoriser les produits locaux et à ouvrir des perspectives économiques aux femmes rurales. D'après FAO . L’article La Tunisienne Amal Mekni parmi les 100 femmes héroïnes de la FAO est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: PAIDATA : le gouvernement et le FIDA lancent une mission conjointe de supervision
items.description: © DR Le ministre de l'Agriculture Gabriel Mbairobe a présidé le lundi 19 octobre 2026 à Yaoundé le lancement de la mission conjointe de supervision Gouvernement-FIDA du projet d'appui à l'intensification durable de l'agriculture et à la transition agroécologique. Accélérer avant la clôture de mars 2027. L'Administrateur du FODECC, M. Samuel Donatien Nengue, a pris part le lundi 19 octobre 2026 à la cérémonie de lancement de la mission conjointe de supervision Gouvernement-FIDA et d'appui à la mise en œuvre du PAIDATA. La cérémonie, présidée par le ministre de l'Agriculture et du Développement rural, M. Gabriel Mbairobe, s'est tenue dans la salle de conférence du MINADER à Yaoundé. La rencontre a réuni les représentants du MINEPAT, du MINFI, de la Caisse autonome d'amortissement, les responsables des directions du MINADER, ainsi qu'une importante délégation du Fonds international de développement agricole conduite par son directeur pays, M. Eric Rwabidadi. Les responsables du PAIDATA, de l'IRAD et d'autres projets bénéficiant des financements du FODECC étaient également présents. Prévue du 19 au 30 octobre 2026, cette mission a pour objectifs d'évaluer les performances du projet, d'examiner les réalisations techniques et financières, d'identifier les contraintes opérationnelles et de formuler des recommandations pour renforcer l'efficacité des interventions sur le terrain. À cette occasion, l'Administrateur du FODECC a présenté l'état d'avancement des diligences engagées pour satisfaire aux conditions de décaissement des ressources additionnelles du partenariat CAFI. Il a réaffirmé les efforts pour accélérer les procédures administratives et renforcer la justification des résultats, avec pour ambition de mobiliser les ressources disponibles avant la clôture du projet, prévue en mars 2027. Autre perspective majeure : la finance verte. M. Samuel Donatien Nengue a également évoqué les préparatifs liés à cette orientation stratégique, qui doit positionner le FODECC au cœur du financement de la transition agroécologique. Cet article PAIDATA : le gouvernement et le FIDA lancent une mission conjointe de supervision est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Hamzat mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti, says legacy will endure
items.description: The Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, has described the death of Pa Reuben Fasoranti, former National Leader of Afenifere, as a profound loss to the Yoruba race and Nigeria. Hamzat expressed his condolences in a message signed by Mr Tunde Alao, Senior Special Assistant to the Governor (Media), Office of the Deputy Governor, on Wednesday in Lagos. He extended his heartfelt sympathies, on behalf of his family, to the Fasoranti family, the government and people of Ondo State, and the entire Yoruba race over the death of the elder statesman at the age of 100. The deputy governor described Fasoranti as a distinguished educator, principled leader and respected voice in Nigeria’s socio-political landscape, whose life was devoted to justice, fairness and the preservation of Yoruba values within a united Nigeria. According to him, Fasoranti’s leadership of Afenifere reflected his unwavering commitment to the dignity, rights and aspirations of the Yoruba people. He said the late elder statesman’s courage, wisdom and steadfast adherence to principle earned him the respect of generations, making him a father figure, counsellor and custodian of enduring values in Yoruba leadership. “Pa Fasoranti lived a remarkable century of service to his people and humanity. His life was defined by integrity, conviction and an enduring commitment to justice. “He was a voice of wisdom whose counsel and principles will continue to inspire generations to come,” Hamzat said. The deputy governor noted that Fasoranti’s death was a significant loss not only to his immediate family and Ondo State but also to the Yoruba nation and Nigeria as a whole. He added that the late leader’s legacy of selfless service and principled leadership would remain a source of inspiration for generations to come. While acknowledging the grief occasioned by his death, the deputy governor urged the bereaved family and the Yoruba people to draw comfort from the enduring impact of Fasoranti’s life, the values he upheld and the many lives he touched. He prayed that Almighty God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give his family, loved ones and all those mourning his passing the strength and fortitude to bear the loss. (NAN) The post Hamzat mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti, says legacy will endure appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: El Constitucional rechaza el amparo por la ‘ley de nietos’ y deja en el aire el voto de 160.000 españoles
items.description: El pleno del Tribunal Constitucional, por diez votos a dos, ha inadmitido el recurso del Defensor del Pueblo que pedía restablecer el derecho al voto de 160.000 nacionalizados a quienes el Tribunal Supremo suspendió el sufragio el pasado 12 de octubre, día de la Hispanidad. Una mayoría del tribunal de garantías, más allá de la división de referencia entre progresistas y conservadores, ha considerado que, como el procedimiento sigue abierto en el Supremo —hasta pasado mañana, viernes, aún pueden personarse los afectados—, el recurso del Defensor es “prematuro” y que incumple el requisito de subsidiariedad del amparo: esto es, que se hayan agotado todas las vías de la justicia ordinaria. Dos magistrados progresistas emitirán un voto particular en contra de la decisión mayoritaria y en defensa de un derecho fundamental, el sufragio, que el Defensor considera restringido sin intervención del legislador ni tampoco por ningún acto atribuible a los afectados. items.title: PSG : Kvaratskhelia, gravement blessé au genou droit, absent plusieurs mois
items.description: L'attaquant du PSG Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, blessé mardi contre le FC Barcelone, est « victime d'une rupture du ligament croisé antérieur du genou droit » et sera absent plusieurs mois, a annoncé mercredi le club. Ousmane Dembélé, blessé à la cuisse gauche, « restera en soins ces prochaines semaines » comme Marquinhos, touché à la cuisse droite, a précisé le PSG dans un communiqué médical, après la victoire (4-2) mardi à domicile face au Barça en Ligue des champions. Pour rappel, une semaine après avoir fait tomber Manchester City (4-2) sur sa pelouse, le PSG a enchaîné un troisième succès en autant de rencontres européennes en dominant 4-2 Barcelone mardi au Parc des Princes lors d'un choc spectaculaire en Ligue des champions. Après l'ouverture du score par Désiré Doué (38e), le Barça a répondu avec Xavi Espart (55e), avant que Lucas Hernandez ne redonne l'avantage au PSG de la tête (72e). L'inévitable Lamine Yamal (79e) a de nouveau égalisé mais Vitinha (81e) et Fabian Ruiz (86e) ont fait pincer les Blaugranas, leur infligeant leur première défaite de la saison. items.title: ‘Don’t treat it as an Obuasi episode’ – Kofi Asare calls for school safeguarding reforms
items.description: The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, has called on the Ghana Education Service (GES), the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Gender to use the sexual abuse scandal at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) as an opportunity to reform safeguarding systems across the country. He said the allegations should not be treated as an isolated incident involving one school but as a wake-up call for a broader review of how sexual abuse complaints are handled and how students are protected in Ghanaian schools. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show during a discussion on the Obuasi SHTS scandal, Mr Asare said the most important outcome should be lasting changes to the system rather than a response limited to the case. “For me, the most important thing in all this is that the GES, the Ministry of Education, and the Ministry of Gender; these three agencies should not see what is happening as an Obuasi episode,” he said. “No. We should see this as an opportunity to undertake system-wide reforms in safeguarding in Ghana.” Mr Asare acknowledged that scandals could occur in any country but said the response to such incidents determined whether institutions learnt from them and prevented similar cases in the future. He warned that treating the Obuasi case as an isolated incident would mean missing an opportunity to address weaknesses in the systems responsible for protecting students. “In every country, you know, scandals happen. But the most important thing is what countries, what nations make out of these scandals,” he said. “If we reduce it to a case, then we’ve lost it.” Mr Asare said one of the key reforms needed was to move safeguarding responses away from the direct control of the GES and place them under an external agency. He said that relying on the same institution to handle complaints and oversee responses could make it difficult to address persistent weaknesses in the system. He said Africa Education Watch had proposed an arrangement that would give an independent body responsibility for responding to safeguarding concerns in schools. “We should see this as a launchpad to undertake system-level reforms in safeguarding in our schools,” he said. He added that the proposed changes should include “feeding safeguarding responses to an external agency other than the GES system”. According to him, such a move would help address recurring problems instead of allowing the same issues to emerge repeatedly without meaningful reform. Mr Asare also welcomed the decision by the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to withdraw Zakaria Abdullahi from the party’s election in Juaben, but said this should have been taken without the need for sustained public pressure and advocacy. “I mean, the person has withdrawn. It is good,” he said. However, Mr Asare expressed concern that the decision came only after considerable pressure from campaigners and other concerned groups. “Unfortunately, it had to come on the back of strenuous advocacy and pressure. Well, we welcome the decision. But the standards for me are the most important for our democracy,” he said. He warned that Ghana was likely to encounter similar cases in the future, including situations involving people with political connections or links to political parties. “We will definitely meet similar cases in the future where people who are politically connected or politically associated persons participate in illegal activities in our school environment. Definitely, we will meet those cases,” he said. Mr Asare said the way political parties respond to such incidents would help establish standards for dealing with future cases. He said that taking a clear position when concerns first arise would make it easier for political parties and institutions to respond consistently when similar situations occur. “And so when you have good precedent, it makes it easier for the next incident to follow suit,” he said. While welcoming the NDC’s decision, Mr Asare said that the party should not have waited for public pressure before taking action. “But it shouldn’t have come on the back of pressure and advocacy. It should have been an easier decision to take in the interest of the parties,” he said.
