items.title: OTE | La Tunisie s’enfonce dans la spirale de l’endettement
items.description: Dans le contexte des discussions en cours sur la crise de l’endettement, à l’occasion des réunions annuelles du Fonds monétaire international (FMI) et de la Banque mondiale (BM), l’Observatoire tunisien de l’économie (OTE) a republié son rapport en arabe intitulé : «La spirale de l’endettement en Tunisie : 35 prêts en deux années parlementaires», consultable sur son site web . Ce rapport met en lumière le volume des prêts approuvés au cours des années parlementaires 2023/2024 et 2024/2025, ainsi que les bailleurs de fonds et les conditions d’emprunt. Il interroge, par ailleurs, les répercussions de ces engagements sur la souveraineté financière et sur les priorités économiques et sociales en Tunisie. Nous traduisons ci-dessous l'introduction et la conclusion de cette étude. Au cours de la dernière décennie, la Tunisie a connu une série de crises économiques et financières, aggravées par un endettement devenu un lourd fardeau pour les Tunisiens, qui pèse sur les générations actuelles et futures. Le volume de la dette publique a atteint des niveaux records, s’élevant à 136 682 millions de dinars en 2024, contre 47 292 millions en 2015. Cette hausse rapide — la dette a triplé en dix ans — reflète une politique gouvernementale caractérisée par une dépendance croissante de l’État à l’égard de l’emprunt pour financer son budget, tout en développant, dans le même temps, un discours soporifique – mais qui n’endort personne, sur le «compter sur soi» et la «souveraineté nationale» . Hausse de l’endettement extérieur et dépendance de l’étranger Entre 2011 et 2024, les ressources empruntées annuellement par la Tunisie pour le financement de son budget ont augmenté d’environ 4 %. Elle a également connu une augmentation de la charge du service de la dette publique, qui a été multipliée par environ six entre 2011 et 2024. Le taux de progression le plus élevé a été enregistré en 2023, atteignant 44,9 %. Cette hausse est principalement due à l’augmentation du remboursement du principal de la dette, consécutive à l’échéance d’emprunts obligataires émis sur les marchés financiers, ainsi qu’à l’accumulation d’importants montants exigibles. Cela résulte d’un recours accru aux emprunts à moyen terme. Depuis 2020, la Tunisie s’est orientée vers un recours croissant à l’emprunt intérieur pour couvrir les besoins budgétaires. La part de la dette intérieure dans les ressources d’emprunt destinées au soutien du budget est ainsi passée d’une moyenne de 30 % sur la période 2015-2019 à une moyenne de 62 % sur la période 2020-2024. Le recours à l’emprunt intérieur a atteint un pic de 82 % en 2024, notamment suite à l’autorisation accordée à la Banque centrale de Tunisie (BCT) d’accorder des facilités au Trésor public pour un montant de 7 000 millions de dinars. Cette évolution s’explique également par un accès limité aux financements extérieurs et par le rétrécissement des options de financement internationales, survenu après la décision de la Tunisie, fin 2020, de cesser tout emprunt auprès du FMI. Dans ce contexte, il devient de plus en plus important de suivre les emprunts approuvés par l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) depuis le début de son mandat en avril 2023 ; en effet, l’endettement constitue un levier auquel l’État a recours pour combler le déficit budgétaire ou financer des projets et programmes publics, compte tenu de la rareté des ressources propres. 64 % de ces emprunts destinés au soutien du budget de l’État Les analyses effectuées dans le cadre de ce rapport ont mis en évidence plusieurs caractéristiques des emprunts approuvés au cours des deux années parlementaires, notamment une forte orientation vers le financement intérieur — qu’il provienne de la BCT ou des banques commerciales — ainsi que l’émergence de nouveaux créanciers pour la Tunisie, suite à l’abandon du recours au FMI. Elles ont par ailleurs révélé que plus de 64 % de ces emprunts étaient destinés au soutien du budget de l’État. Ces prêts étaient assortis de conditions financières parfois onéreuses, dont la sévérité variait selon le créancier. Dans certains cas — comme celui du prêt accordé par le gouvernement italien, dont les conditions sont jugées très favorables (remboursement sur 30 ans et absence d’intérêts) — ces facilités ne sont toutefois pas accordées sans contrepartie ; elles sont liées à des conditions non financières, explicites ou implicites, qui revêtent généralement une dimension politique ou économique. Les documents exposant les motifs des projets de loi relatifs à ces emprunts, ainsi que certains débats au sein de la commission des finances du Parlement, ont révélé l’existence de conditions non financières susceptibles de porter atteinte à la souveraineté de l’État et aux intérêts du pays. Cette perspective demeure néanmoins partielle, car le contrat de prêt n’est généralement pas communiqué aux députés, ce qui donne une vision incomplète de ces conditions. Le processus de ratification des lois relatives aux emprunts au sein de l’Assemblée révèle des défis structurels profonds, liés à la transparence et à la qualité du processus décisionnel en matière d’investissement. La lacune la plus manifeste réside dans l’incapacité structurelle à garantir une transparence suffisante : bien souvent, le projet de loi d’emprunt est soumis sans être accompagné du contrat de prêt lui-même, se limitant à fournir des détails généraux dans l’exposé des motifs. Cette situation empêche les députés ainsi que l’opinion publique d'évaluer avec précision le contenu des accords et leurs conditions réelles. Une «commercialisation trompeuse» des prêts Le défaut majeur réside toutefois dans l’absence d'une logique d’investissement claire et d'un enchaînement cohérent des décisions ; une problématique qui se manifeste dans la manière dont les projets sont programmés, leurs besoins évalués et leur financement assuré. À cela s’ajoute l’émergence d’un phénomène que l’on pourrait qualifier de «commercialisation trompeuse» ( mismarketing ) des prêts : les objectifs de ces derniers sont reformulés, voire politiquement amplifiés, afin de paraître alignés sur des priorités populaires — comme c’est le cas pour les crédits destinés aux projets d’énergies renouvelables. Malgré la répétition de ces critiques, elles n’aboutissent que rarement au rejet des emprunts ou à une modification substantielle de leur contenu. Au cours de deux législatures, tous les emprunts soumis au Parlement ont été approuvés, à une seule exception près sur un total de 34 dossiers. Cela témoigne de la portée limitée du rôle de contrôle du Parlement, une situation qui s’explique structurellement par les restrictions imposées par la Constitution à ses prérogatives. Le Parlement se limitant à approuver ou à rejeter les accords — sans pouvoir formuler de réserves ni exiger du gouvernement une révision — la procédure de ratification parlementaire se réduit, en pratique, à un simple espace d’enregistrement d’observations. Elle ne permet pas d’exercer un véritable pouvoir de veto ou de renégocier les conditions, surtout en l’absence de clauses garantissant la transparence ou exigeant une concertation préalable. L’article OTE | La Tunisie s'enfonce dans la spirale de l’endettement est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Manifestations du 24 octobre en France : un dispositif de sécurité «massif» annoncé
items.description: Face aux critiques sur le maintien de l'ordre lors de la journee de mobilisation du 17 octobre , le Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu et le ministre de l'Interieur Laurent Nuñez ont detaille, le 20 octobre a l'Assemblee nationale, les mesures prevues pour les nouvelles manifestations du 24 octobre. Plus de moyens, plus de mobilite et l'appui de l'armee « Le dispositif de samedi prochain sera massif », a declare le chef du gouvernement devant les deputes, reconnaissant que celui du 17 octobre avait ete « trop statique et pas assez mobile ». "Samedi prochain, le dispositif sera massif", indique @SebLecornu avant de critiquer la "démagogie" et les "coups de menton". #QAG https://t.co/h4Jihdjoen — LCP (@LCP) October 20, 2026 Laurent Nuñez a precise : « Nous allons evidemment monter en gamme […] en termes de moyens, en volume bien sûr, en termes de forces engagees et en termes de reactivite, de mobilite, pour aller percuter, impacter ces groupes qui dispersent les forces de l'ordre de maniere extremement planifiee ». Manifs - Acte II : le ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez annonce le déploiement samedi #24octobre des unités de l'opération militaire Sentinelle de l'armée pour libérer des policiers de leurs missions de garde statique. https://t.co/tnvKGy9opX — Infos Françaises (@InfosFrancaises) October 20, 2026 Seront mobilises la Brigade de recherche et d'intervention, le Groupe d'intervention de la Gendarmerie nationale, le RAID (Recherche, assistance, intervention, dissuasion), des helicopteres, des Centaures et des engins lanceurs d'eau. Les militaires de l'operation Sentinelle seront en outre deployes « en substitution des forces de securite interieure, principalement sur des missions de securisation statique », afin de liberer policiers et gendarmes pour le maintien de l'ordre. Sur X, le depute de La France insoumise, Bastien Lachaud, a vivement reagi : « En annoncant le deploiement de Sentinelle […], Laurent Nuñez franchit un nouveau seuil dans la surenchere securitaire. L'armee n'a pas vocation a etre utilisee contre son propre peuple ». 🚨 ALERTE ! Laurent Nuñez annonce le déploiement de militaires de l’opération Sentinelle pour la manifestation du 24 octobre. Les manifestants ne doivent pas être considéré comme des ennemis de l'intérieur ! L’armée doit défendre la Nation, pas faire du maintien de l'ordre. Cette confusion des genres est dangereuse. — Bastien Lachaud (@LachaudB) October 20, 2026 Le ministre a par ailleurs indique qu'il reflechissait a l'interdiction de manifestations non declarees ou susceptibles de troubler l'ordre public, y compris certaines pourtant declarees si le service d'ordre ne garantit pas la securite. Pour les corteges sans risque, il juge imperatif de privilegier des itineraires eloignes des bâtiments publics et des rues commercantes. Il souhaite aussi renforcer le renseignement sur les participants les plus radicaux. « Nous serons au rendez-vous », a-t-il assure, en promettant la fermete.

items.title: DVLA warns public against fake SMS payment links and online fine scams
items.description: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) has warned the public against fraudulent text messages and online payment links used by scammers to collect money from unsuspecting motorists under the pretext of paying fines. In a public notice issued on Wednesday, October 21, the Authority said it had noted with concern the activities of fraudsters sending fake SMS messages to members of the public while pretending to collect fines on its behalf. The DVLA said the scammers send text messages containing links that redirect recipients to fake websites or payment platforms, where they are asked to pay fines they allegedly owe the Authority. According to the Authority, some of the messages create a sense of urgency by setting payment deadlines or promising discounts to persuade recipients to make payments without verifying the claims. The DVLA has, however, dismissed the messages as fraudulent and urged the public to disregard them. “The DVLA wishes to categorically inform the general public that these messages are fraudulent and must be disregarded,” the notice stated. The Authority stressed that it does not offer discounts on fines, warning motorists to be cautious of any message, website or individual claiming otherwise. “The DVLA does not offer discounts on fines. Any SMS, website, platform, or person claiming to offer discounted DVLA fines is fraudulent,” it said. The warning is intended to alert the public to the tactics used by fraudsters, who may rely on attractive offers and pressure to make people act quickly without checking whether a payment request is genuine. The DVLA advised motorists not to assume that a message is legitimate simply because it refers to a fine or appears to come from an official source. It urged anyone who receives such messages to verify the information through the Authority’s recognised communication channels before taking any action. The DVLA has also clarified that the only acceptable online payment gateway for its transactions is the Government of Ghana’s official payment platform, Ghana.gov.gh. It said members of the public should treat any other website or unofficial payment link claiming to represent the Authority as fake. The DVLA identified its official website as www.dvla.gov.gh and urged the public to use it to verify information relating to its services and transactions. “The only acceptable online payment gateway for DVLA transactions is the Government of Ghana’s official payment platform, https://www.Ghana.gov.gh,” the notice said. The Authority added that any website, shortened link or other online platform claiming to represent the DVLA outside its approved channels should be treated with suspicion. As part of measures to protect the public against the scams, the DVLA has advised motorists not to click on suspicious links, disclose personal information or make payments through unofficial platforms. It also urged the public to confirm all information relating to its services through its official website, recognised DVLA offices and approved public communication channels. The Authority said anyone who receives a suspicious text message should report it to the nearest DVLA office or the appropriate law enforcement agency for further investigation and action.

items.title: AFENIFERE RIFT: Those still making noise in cuckoo land – Omololu
items.description: By Dickson Omobola National Organising Secretary of Afenifere, Abagun Omololu, has expressed optimism about the future of the pan-Yoruba socio-cultural organisation after the death of its leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, saying those still making noise on the sidelines are crying in a cloud of cuckoo land. Recall that in the build-up to the 2023 general elections, which brought President Bola Tinubu to power, acting leader of Afenifere, the late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, supported Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, while the substantive leader, Fasoranti, supported Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, causing a division within the organisation. Speaking on The Morning Show, an Arise TV programme, Wednesday, Omololu described the period as unfortunate, saying such a development had never occurred in Yorubaland. He said: “It is an unfortunate period that we had before the 2023 election that got the acting leader and the substantive leader backing separate candidates. It’s an unfortunate thing. It had never happened in the history of Yorubaland.” On the future of Afenifere, he said: “The future of Afenifere is fantastic. Somebody came to be appointed a leader. The era of Baba Adebanjo is gone. Whoever that is still making noise on the side, I see it as a cry in a cloud of cuckoo land.” On Fasoranti’s legacy, he said: “To those of us who are very close to Baba, we have lost something in humanity. An embodiment of contentment, of somebody who sees public service as a sacrifice. Baba graduated from the University of Ibadan in 1951. There were not many graduates then. Immediately, he became a part of the Action Group of the late Obafemi Awolowo. He was a young man of 25 years old. Not many of his contemporaries were graduates. “Baba (Awolowo) pulled him, he worked with the likes of Professor Aluko, Professor Aboyade Cole and the rest. These are phenomenal leaders who came to the world for service. That is what Baba is for us. There was a time Baba lost his wife. Now he used to be made the governor of Ondo State, which a lot of people are dying for. They are using drug money, they are using everything now to buy the position. “The position was presented on the platter of gold to Baba, but he said, no, I cannot be a governor without having a wife, and I’m not ready to marry again. What a human being. Baba refused the position. That is why the position went to Baba Adefarati. This is a kind of human being. Baba’s life was Awoism. It’s not something where you march to gain political attention. It’s an inborn thing in him. We are going to serve the less privileged. That is what Baba is all about and Awoism. Egalitarian society. Let the rich get richer, while the poor must be looked after. These fingers are not equal. That is why they call us welfarists. That’s what Baba stood for. All his life. That was what Awolowo handed over to us.” The post AFENIFERE RIFT: Those still making noise in cuckoo land – Omololu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UFOA-B U17: le Burkina échoue encore aux portes de la CAN
items.description: Battus 1-0 par le Niger en demi-finale du tournoi qualificatif de l’UFOA-B, le mardi 20 octobre 2026, au stade du 4-Août de Ouagadougou, les Étalons cadets manquent la qualification pour la CAN U17 pour la deuxième édition consécutive. Une nouvelle désillusion pour le football burkinabè. Le rêve continental s’est brisé à domicile pour les Étalons U17 du Burkina Faso. Opposés au Mena du Niger, le mardi 20 octobre 2026, au stade du 4-Août de Ouagadougou, en demi-finale du tournoi qualificatif de l’Union des fédérations ouest-africaines de football (UFOA-B), les jeunes Burkinabè se sont inclinés sur le score de 1 but à 0. Cette défaite est synonyme d’élimination pour les cadets burkinabè, qui voient ainsi s’envoler leurs espoirs de disputer la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) U17. Évoluant devant leur public, les Étalons n’ont pas réussi à franchir cet obstacle décisif face à leurs homologues nigériens. Le coup est d’autant plus dur que le Burkina Faso manque la phase finale continentale pour la deuxième édition consécutive. Une nouvelle désillusion pour le football cadet burkinabè, qui devra encore patienter avant de retrouver la grande scène africaine de cette catégorie. Un bilan qui laisse des regrets Au terme de cette campagne qualificative, les Étalons U17 affichent un bilan de quatre matchs disputés, une victoire contre le Togo, deux matchs nuls et une défaite, concédée face au Niger. Sur le plan offensif et défensif, les statistiques sont tout aussi révélatrices: un seul but inscrit contre deux encaissés sur l’ensemble du tournoi. Un bilan qui n’aura pas suffi aux jeunes Burkinabè pour atteindre leur objectif. Avec cette élimination, les Étalons cadets quittent donc la compétition sans billet pour la prochaine CAN U17. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article UFOA-B U17: le Burkina échoue encore aux portes de la CAN est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Stop! Go! Stop Again! The NDC’S three-day course in political principles (Updated)
items.description: (When a Political Party cannot decide whether to protect its principles or its own aspirant ) By Jimmy Aglah Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, there lived a traffic policeman whose understanding of road safety depended entirely on which vehicle was approaching. When a stranger arrived, he stepped into the road, raised his palm and ordered him to stop. When his brother appeared, he waved him through with great enthusiasm. But when the public began asking questions, he raised his palm again and ordered everybody to stop. The confused motorists complained to his superior, who congratulated him for demonstrating remarkable flexibility in traffic management. Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the latest episode of Ghana’s political circus, starring the National Democratic Congress and featuring one Zakaria Abdulai, the interdicted headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. On Sunday, 18 October, the NDC announced that Abdulai must withdraw from the Juaben Constituency chairmanship contest or face disqualification. Wonderful! The traffic light was red, and public confidence briefly found somewhere to park. By Monday, however, the party had discovered another colour. After hearing from Abdulai, its Functional Executive Committee decided he could contest after all. The traffic light turned green. The explanation was natural justice, constitutional rights and the presumption of innocence. Then came Tuesday, 20 October. Following further consideration, the party discovered that transparency and accountability were also important principles. The traffic light returned to red. Abdulai subsequently resigned as constituency secretary and withdrew from the chairmanship race. Three days, three positions! Even the most confused trotro driver at Kejetia would have demanded directions. But let us not mistake the comedy of political indecision for the gravity of the underlying matter. Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow , examines disturbing allegations of sexual harassment, assault and rape involving female students. Manasseh initially reported that the number of students alleging abuse had risen to at least sixteen. These are serious accusations, not established findings of guilt. Abdulai deserves a fair investigation and the presumption of innocence. Yet this is precisely where the NDC’s political gymnastics become difficult to defend. Nobody is suggesting that a political party should operate a criminal court. But must a man be convicted before an organisation exercises reasonable caution over who represents its leadership? The Ghana Education Service interdicted the headmaster pending investigations. It did not need a judicial verdict to recognise the importance of safeguarding students and protecting public confidence. Apparently, the NDC initially required a different kind of mathematics, where the seriousness of allegations must first be divided by the political rights of an aspirant, multiplied by internal electoral timetables and then referred to the Functional Executive Committee for further calculation. The party’s eventual decision was welcome, but its journey there was an extraordinary exhibition of institutional wobbling. And just when the Republic thought the drama had exhausted its supply of surprises, Interior Minister Mohammed Mubarak Muntaka introduced another development. Appearing before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, the Minister disclosed that Abdulai had been arrested and questioned by the police. He explained that he had earlier directed the investigation to be transferred from the Ashanti Region to Police Headquarters in Accra. Investigators were also pursuing court authorisation to obtain DNA evidence. Now, this is where the story becomes particularly instructive. While the NDC was busy changing the political traffic lights, the criminal investigation was taking a more consequential course. An arrest, of course, is not a conviction, and DNA testing must follow the law. But surely a political party need not wait until police investigations become headline news before recognising the wisdom of reasonable precautions. The police, at least, were pursuing evidence. The party, meanwhile, had spent three days pursuing consensus with its own previous decisions. Meanwhile, the Ghana Education Service has directed the Ashanti Regional Director of Education and the Obuasi Municipal Director to step aside while investigations continue. The Service says the decision is intended to prevent interference or even the perception of interference. It has also reminded the public that the headmaster remains interdicted and has not been cleared. Was there negligence in the earlier handling of complaints? Were allegations inadequately investigated? Did personal influence or institutional loyalty obstruct accountability? These are questions for investigators, not verdicts for newspaper columns. But they deserve answers, especially where the protection of students may have been compromised. An Akan elder might remind us that when a child cries and points towards the forest, the wise adult investigates before dismissing the cry as an inconvenience. Unfortunately, Ghanaian institutions sometimes behave as though the greatest danger is not what might have happened to the child, but what might happen to the reputation of the adult being investigated. And here lies the NDC’s real problem. A governing party that proclaims accountability cannot afford to treat ethical leadership like a funeral contribution, offered generously when the cameras are present and reconsidered when the family meeting begins. Fairness is indispensable. So is the protection of complainants. Natural justice must never become a convenient excuse for institutional paralysis, just as public outrage must never replace due process. For the students of Obuasi SHTS, the message must be unmistakable: their safety, dignity and right to be heard matter more than anybody’s constituency ambitions. For the NDC, the lesson should be equally unmistakable. Political credibility is not preserved merely by correcting a questionable decision. It also depends on the judgement that produced the decision in the first place. Abdulai has now withdrawn from the contest, and the police investigation continues. The allegations must be tested through a fair and independent process. That is how justice is served, not through rumours, political pressure or premature declarations of innocence or guilt. The party has finally found its brakes. Congratulations! But when a political organisation needs three traffic signals in three days to discover where it should stop, while the police are busy pursuing evidence, perhaps the problem is not merely with the driver. Someone should urgently inspect the steering committee. Welcome to the Republic of Uncommon Sense, where political principles sometimes change faster than the traffic lights, and common sense must apply for clearance before entering the constituency office.

items.title: From Potential to Practice: Africa’s AI decade has begun
items.description: A month after PAAIS 2026, the summit’s convenor reflects on what the room revealed and what leaders in boardrooms and ministries must do now. Watching the highlights film from this year’s Pan African AI & Innovation Summit, I was struck less by the stage than by the people in the audience. Bankers beside students. Regulators beside founders. Civil servants taking notes next to engineers who build the very systems those civil servants will one day have to govern. For two days in Accra, people who rarely shared a room faced a shared problem and treated it as their own. That, in a sentence, is why the Pan African AI & Innovation Summit exists. The audience no longer For too long, the global story of artificial intelligence may have cast Africa as the audience. Models are trained elsewhere on data that rarely reflects our languages, markets, or people, then arrive here as finished products to be adopted, priced, and regulated after the fact. The risk is that we live inside it on terms that are written by someone else. What I heard across the keynotes and corridor conversations this September was a refusal of that role. Africa will not wait to see how AI unfolds globally. We are deciding how it will serve our economies, our institutions and our people. The gap we must name Ambition is often perceived by many as readiness, but it’s not, and honesty demands that we say so. Ahead of the summit, PAAIS surveyed 100 professionals from 89 institutions in preparation for our AI masterclass in partnership with the Chartered Institute of Bankers Ghana. 65% said their organisations were still at the pre-pilot stage. 68% had no AI governance committee. Most strikingly, 18 of the 35 organisations already piloting or scaling AI were doing so without one. Read that again. Half of the institutions already putting AI in front of customers have no formal body asking who is accountable when it goes wrong. And the outcome respondents wanted most, chosen by 50%, was a governance framework their boards could use. This is not a story of reluctance. It is a story of people moving faster than the structures meant to protect them and the public they serve. Closing that gap is precisely the work a convening like ours is built for. Why the room matters Policy developed without industry input can never be truly complete. Likewise, an industry that advances without policy rests on a fragile foundation. And when both are shaped without young people at the table, they risk building a future for a generation they never consulted. In Africa, home to the youngest population in the world, the voices, ideas, and aspirations of young people are essential to creating sustainable and inclusive progress. PAAIS rests on four commitments: equipping young people with skills, strengthening policy and digital sovereignty, unlocking partnership and investment, and insisting that AI be applied ethically in the sectors closest to daily life, namely health, agriculture, education and finance. None of these works alone. A skilled graduate without an investor stalls. A brilliant regulation that no one in industry understands gathers dust. Investment without ethical guardrails eventually costs more trust than it earns. The summit’s purpose is to hold these forces in the same room long enough for them to discover they need each other. What I ask of leaders To business leaders: establish AI governance before your next pilot, not after your first incident. Your board deserves a framework, and your customers deserve to know that someone is accountable. To technology leaders: build for the user in Kumasi as seriously as the user in London. Local language, local data and local context. They are the product. To government institutions: We are grateful that our leaders are increasingly recognising convening as critical infrastructure. The regulators who engage founders, innovators, and industry leaders before drafting policy invariably create stronger, more practical, and future-ready frameworks. As several Ministers highlighted during the summit, digital sovereignty is about where data is stored. Equally, it is also about whether we possess the capability, expertise, and confidence to make strategic decisions for ourselves. True sovereignty is built on infrastructure, competence, ownership, and the capacity to shape our own technological destiny. The human reality It would be easy to write about AI entirely in numbers. But the energy in that hall was not statistical. It was hope, carefully tested. People did not come to be dazzled by technology. They came to find out whether it could be made to work for the nurse, the farmer, the bank teller and the young person they know by name. The summit lasted two days. The work it began will take a generation. No one will hand Africa an AI future that fits us. We are building it together, in rooms like that one, to solve our own challenges and then carry it back into our boardrooms, ministries and classrooms. The conversation continues toward PAAIS 2027. I invite every leader reading this to take a seat at the table.

items.title: Anambra Assembly passes State Police Bill
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to amend relevant provisions of the 1999 Constitution to pave the way for the establishment of state police in Nigeria. The bill passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary in Awka on Tuesday, marking a step towards establishing a constitutional framework for decentralised policing in the country. The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, seeks to provide a legal basis for states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and an Act of the National Assembly prescribing minimum national policing standards. Under the proposed framework, the Nigeria Police Force would remain the default policing institution in a state until a state police service is lawfully established and certified operational. The bill also retains the Federal Government’s policing responsibilities across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, while providing safeguards for civilian oversight, human rights protection, national policing standards, independent police service commissions, intergovernmental cooperation, criminal information systems and firearms control. It further provides for exceptional federal intervention in state policing in cases involving institutional breakdown, serious incapacity, threats to national security or grave abuses. At the plenary, presided over by the Speaker, Dr Somtochukwu Udeze, the lawmakers adopted the bill through a voice vote. Speaking after the adoption, Udeze said the House had fulfilled its constitutional responsibility and directed the Clerk of the Assembly to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly. The Majority Leader of the House, Mr Ikenna Ofodeme, described state police as necessary, arguing that many security challenges originate at the grassroots. He disagreed with critics who fear that state police could be abused, saying the arrangement would enable state authorities to respond more quickly to security threats rather than wait for directives from the Inspector-General of Police. According to him, establishing state police would strengthen efforts to tackle insecurity and create employment opportunities for young people. Ofodeme also said the arrangement could reduce pressure on the military, which is frequently deployed to support the police in addressing internal security challenges. He suggested that local vigilantes could be integrated into the policing system and given appropriate training to improve community-level security. He maintained that a state police structure would bring policing closer to the people and improve the speed of security responses. items.title: Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain
items.description: The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain, which is behind a major DR Congo outbreak , and the patient is a diplomat, an emergency meeting heard on Wednesday. The case in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda to the capital Abuja on Oct 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said. Since the Ebola outbreak was declared in the Democratic Republic of Congo in mid-May, the deadly viral haemorrhagic fever has spread to several countries across the continent, including to neighbouring Uganda. “We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, director of the public health laboratory service at the NCDC said. The World Health Organisation (WHO) also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain , for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. “This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said, adding the patient has deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”. The director general of Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, warned on Tuesday of “an extremely serious threat” as Kenya also declared its ninth Ebola case. In several months, the DRC’s Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country’s history, killing 4,381 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases, according to the health authorities. Nigeria has identified 44 contacts that are being monitored, while intensifying efforts to find other people who may have been exposed. The WHO said in a statement that infection prevention and control was being “ramped up” at the private hospital where the patient sought care.

items.title: Finance Ministry to meet maritime stakeholders over Tema Port clearance delays
items.description: The Ministry of Finance will meet key stakeholders in Ghana’s maritime and logistics sectors on Wednesday, October 21, to discuss proposed changes to customs clearance procedures amid concerns about persistent delays and rising costs at Tema Port. The meeting will review existing cargo clearance processes and consider proposed amendments aimed at addressing operational challenges affecting the smooth and timely movement of goods. The engagement follows calls by the Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) for urgent intervention over delays in shipping invoices, payment processing and container releases. The Association says the bottlenecks are increasing demurrage, rent and storage charges for businesses operating through the port. IEAG has also raised concerns about reported disruptions at Meridian Port Services (MPS) Terminal 3, where more than 120 trucks scheduled to transfer containers were reportedly delayed. It warned that the situation could extend truck turnaround times, disrupt haulage schedules and increase operating costs for importers and other port users, calling for an investigation to establish the causes and determine responsibility. In an invitation signed by Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem on behalf of the Finance Minister, the Ministry said its Revenue Policy Division had conducted a preliminary assessment of existing customs clearance procedures and identified operational challenges affecting cargo movement. The Ministry said the stakeholder meeting would provide an opportunity to discuss and review proposed amendments. Expected participants include the Ghana Revenue Authority, Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority, Ghana Shippers’ Authority, Ghana Link Network Services, Meridian Port Services Limited, industry associations and other maritime sector stakeholders.

items.title: LdC : Bayern-Arsenal, le Real Madrid en action, Lille et Lens sous pression
items.description: La troisième journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions se termine ce mercredi avec neuf rencontres au programme. Le choc entre le Bayern Munich et Arsenal sera particulièrement attendu, tandis que le Real Madrid cherchera à poursuivre son parcours européen. Lille et Lens tenteront, de leur côté, de relancer leur campagne. La Ligue des champions promet une nouvelle soirée animée ce mercredi 21 octobre. Neuf rencontres sont au programme de cette troisième journée, avec plusieurs affiches à suivre de près. Le Bayern Munich reçoit Arsenal dans l’un des chocs les plus attendus, tandis que le Real Madrid sera également en lice face au RB Leipzig. Les clubs français Lille et Lens chercheront, quant à eux, à rebondir après leurs dernières déconvenues européennes. Le Bayern Munich accueille Arsenal dans un duel entre deux prétendants au titre européen. Les Bavarois abordent cette rencontre après une large victoire contre le RB Leipzig (6-1) en Bundesliga, tandis que les Gunners restent sur un succès face à Nottingham Forest (1-0). Arsenal affiche une dynamique solide, avec dix victoires en onze rencontres officielles cette saison. Le club londonien avait également marqué les esprits en dominant Lille (3-0) lors de la précédente journée européenne. Le Bayern devra donc se montrer à la hauteur face à une équipe en confiance. L’absence potentielle de Vincent Kompany, malade, et la suspension de Michael Olise pourraient toutefois compliquer la tâche des Munichois. Le Real Madrid face au RB Leipzig Le Real Madrid reçoit le RB Leipzig avec l’ambition de poursuivre sa campagne européenne et de conforter sa position dans la phase de ligue. Le club espagnol, habitué aux grands rendez-vous continentaux, sera attendu devant son public face à une formation allemande qui cherchera à créer la surprise. Cette rencontre représente un test important pour les Madrilènes, qui devront faire preuve de sérieux pour éviter de laisser des points en route. Face à un adversaire capable de se montrer dangereux, le Real cherchera à imposer son rythme et à faire valoir son expérience européenne. Lille et Lens veulent relancer leur campagne Le LOSC reçoit Galatasaray avec l’objectif de décrocher ses premiers points dans cette phase de ligue. Les deux équipes restent sur une défaite lors de la précédente journée : Lille s’est incliné face à Arsenal (3-0), tandis que Galatasaray a été battu par le FC Barcelone (4-1). De son côté, le RC Lens se déplace en Belgique pour affronter le Club Bruges. Après avoir débuté la compétition par une victoire contre le Slavia Prague (3-2), les Sang et Or ont perdu face au Sporting Portugal (2-0). Le club nordiste espère retrouver une dynamique positive après deux succès en championnat contre Lyon (2-1) et Troyes (3-1). items.title: NDPC DG urges action on existing policies to boost Ghana’s human capital
items.description: The Director-General of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, has called on stakeholders to focus on implementing existing policies and commitments to build a productive human capital ecosystem in Ghana. She said the country already had policies, institutions and legislative frameworks to support human capital development, stressing that the priority should be to translate these commitments into practical outcomes rather than continually developing new policy documents. Dr Amoah made the remarks at the sixth annual Precision Policy Conference on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, under the theme “Human Capital at Work.” “Please, let us work with what we have and translate these existing commitments into tangible change,” she said. She explained that human capital development required coordinated action across health, early childhood development, education, skills training, employment and enterprise development to ensure that people acquired relevant skills and applied them productively. The NDPC Director-General also emphasised the need for adequate financing, monitoring, evaluation and learning to ensure that policies translated into measurable improvements in people’s lives. “Let us move from policy to plans, from plans to budgets, and from commitments to implementation,” she said. Dr Amoah expressed hope that the conference would generate practical recommendations to strengthen the proposed Human Capital Development Strategy and connect the various policy areas into a coherent and productive ecosystem. The Founder and President of the Design and Technology Institute (DTI), Constance Swaniker, said Ghana’s ambition to become a high-income nation by 2057 would depend on the productivity and capabilities of its people. She cited the World Bank’s Human Capital Index, noting that a child born in Ghana today was expected to attain about 45 per cent of the productivity potential associated with full health and quality education. Ms Swaniker urged stakeholders to view human capital as a productive asset, arguing that development efforts must consider not only educational qualifications but also people’s ability to contribute meaningfully to the economy. “Human capital is built by all of us, or it is not built at all,” she said, highlighting the shared responsibility of government, industry, academia, development partners and young people.

items.title: Nigeria already a failed state, middle class gone — Duke
items.description: PRP candidate blames poverty, unemployment for kidnapping, banditry The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has described Nigeria as a failed state, citing worsening poverty, unemployment, insecurity and economic decline. Duke said he decided to contest the 2027 presidential election because he could no longer remain on the sidelines while the country’s challenges deepened without offering himself as an alternative. Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, the former Cross River State governor said he was driven by what he described as the urgency of rescuing Nigeria from its current trajectory. “You get to a point in your life where you say, ‘Either I walk away or I do something.’ “There is no guarantee that you will win. But I don’t want to look back and say that all these things happened and I did nothing,” he said. Duke said Nigeria could not afford another four years of what he described as its present economic and social decline. “I talk about the urgency of now because I don’t think we can go on like this for another four years,” he said. He added that his campaign would focus on policy options and solutions to the country’s challenges rather than personalities. “What I want to do is focus on those who aspire to lead this nation on addressing the issues that affect us and how we can resolve them. “I talk about the options. I talk about the real issues. I don’t want to talk about personalities,” he said. On insecurity, Duke argued that Nigeria’s security challenges could not be separated from the economy’s failure to create enough opportunities for its growing population. “If we don’t address these issues squarely and fundamentally, we’re already a failed state. There’s no question about it. “Look at what is happening — banditry, terrorism, kidnapping and all sorts of conflicts. These are symptoms of a state that is unable, not only to properly articulate its challenges, but to deal with them,” he said. Explaining his assessment, Duke said the existence of a government and public institutions did not necessarily mean that a state was meeting its responsibilities to citizens. “What is the definition of a failed state? Fundamentally, it is a state that fails to meet the aspirations of its people. “You may still have a government and institutions, but if the state cannot protect the people and provide the environment in which they can live productive lives, then it is failing them,” he said. He added that victims of kidnapping would have little reason to be concerned about academic debates over the definition of a failed state when they had experienced the consequences of insecurity. “Talk to someone who has been kidnapped. That person does not need you to explain the definition of a failed state. His experience has already told him what failure of the state means,” he said. Middle class disappearing Duke also lamented what he described as the virtual disappearance of Nigeria’s middle class, arguing that economic pressures had left many households struggling to meet their daily needs. “You have perhaps one per cent who are genuinely wealthy and then a huge number of people struggling around or below the poverty line. “The so-called middle class does not really exist anymore. Many of those we call middle class are only surviving from day-to-day. Let there be one serious emergency and they crumble,” he said. He said businesses were contracting while new enterprises were not emerging fast enough to absorb the growing number of people entering the labour market. “Businesses are contracting. New ones are not springing up the way they should. At the same time, we are turning out graduates every year and adding more people to the working population, but there is no work for them to do,” he said. The PRP candidate also linked poverty and unemployment to kidnapping and banditry, arguing that efforts to tackle insecurity would remain inadequate without addressing the underlying economic conditions. “When it comes to banditry and kidnapping, poverty and unemployment are at the bottom of much of it. “We keep reacting to these crises instead of asking what is producing them. We are too reactive in our governance. Governance is not just about today; it is about laying the foundation for tomorrow,” he said. Oil output, population growth Duke said another issue the presidential campaign should address was whether Nigeria’s economy had expanded sufficiently to support its growing population. Comparing the country’s crude oil production with its population growth, he said Nigeria’s economic capacity had not kept pace with the number of people it needed to support. “In 1980, Nigeria was producing about 2.5 million barrels of oil a day. Forty-six years later, we are producing around 1.7 million barrels, while our population has tripled. “So you have to ask: has the economy expanded enough to carry the population? Clearly, it has not,” he said. He argued that Nigeria’s population should be an economic asset if citizens had access to quality education, employment and opportunities to contribute productively to the economy. “Our numbers ought to be an asset. But a large population is an asset only when you can educate the people, employ them and make them productive,” he said. Duke warned that continued economic hardship could encourage more Nigerians with the means to emigrate, while those remaining in the country faced mounting pressure. Why I returned to Nigeria The presidential candidate said his ambition was also rooted in his decision decades ago to return to Nigeria after studying and working in the United States. “I had the opportunity in my twenties to remain in America. I went to school there and worked there for a while. “But I voluntarily decided that was not where I wanted to be. I believe the Almighty put me in Nigeria for a reason. I believe in this country’s possibilities, and this is where I believe I should contribute,” he said. Duke said the same conviction informed his decision to contest the Cross River governorship election in 1999 and had now motivated him to seek the country’s highest political office. “I wanted to prove then that we were better than what we were putting forward. From experience, I know Nigeria can be a very successful nation,” he said. The post Nigeria already a failed state, middle class gone — Duke appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NDPC boss urges greater use of evaluation evidence in national development planning
items.description: The Director-General of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, has called for greater use of evaluation evidence in national development planning to improve policy implementation, resource allocation and accountability. She made the call at the 2026 Ghana Evaluation Week (GEW) Conference at the University of Ghana, Legon, held under the theme, “Strengthening Evidence Use for Inclusive Development: Bridging Policy, Practice and Innovation.” Dr Amoah said evaluation should go beyond collecting data and producing reports to directly informing policy decisions and delivering measurable development outcomes. “Evaluation must help us identify what works, understand implementation gaps and determine what needs to change to deliver better outcomes for all,” she said. She explained that evidence from the evaluation of the 2022–2025 Medium-Term National Development Policy Framework had informed four strategic shifts in the 2026–2029 framework. These include strengthening institutional and human capital, advancing regulatory and legal reforms, ensuring predictable financing and promoting data-driven coordination. According to Dr Amoah, incorporating evaluation findings into planning processes is essential to ensuring that development policies respond to identified challenges and achieve their intended objectives.

items.title: Crise à la FESABAG : cinq délégations syndicales suspendent leur collaboration avec le Bureau Exécutif
items.description: ​Rien ne va plus au sein de la Fédération Syndicale Autonome des Banques, Assurances et Microfinances de Guinée (FESABAG). Dans une notification adressée le 19 octobre 2026 aux membres du Bureau Exécutif, cinq délégations syndicales de premier plan ont officialisé la suspension de leur collaboration institutionnelle avec la direction actuelle de la faîtière. ​Cette décision a été prise conjointement par les représentants syndicaux de Vista Gui, Access Bank Guinée, AFG Bank Guinée, BPMG et AMIFA Microfinance. ​Dialogue rompu et griefs de gouvernance ​Dans leur courrier, les frondeurs expliquent avoir tenté à plusieurs reprises de privilégier la concertation et de proposer des réformes, notamment par une correspondance restée sans réponse le 17 septembre dernier. Face à ce silence, ils dénoncent des dysfonctionnements profonds qui fragilisent l'organisation depuis la disparition de son ancien dirigeant. ​« Les difficultés observées depuis le décès de notre regretté Camarade Abdoulaye Sow ont soulevé des interrogations sur la continuité institutionnelle, la cohésion interne et la capacité de la Fédération à porter efficacement les préoccupations des travailleurs » , soulignent les signataires. ​Parmi les griefs majeurs avancés par les bases syndicales figurent le manque de transparence, le défaut de redevabilité et le non-respect des textes fondateurs. ​« Les conditions nécessaires à une collaboration institutionnelle sereine avec les instances dirigeantes actuelles ne sont plus réunies », tranche le collectif dans son communiqué. ​Tout en précisant que leur démarche « n'est dirigée contre aucune personne en particulier », les syndicalistes entendent réaffirmer leur attachement à la démocratie interne et aux textes régissant le mouvement syndical en Guinée. ​ « L'unité syndicale ne se décrète pas : elle se construit dans le respect des textes, la concertation et la reconnaissance de la légitimité des représentants des travailleurs » , martèlent-ils. ​La notification de suspension a également été transmise pour information à l'Association Professionnelle des Banques (APB-Guinée), à l'Inspection Générale du Travail (IGT) ainsi qu'aux autres organes professionnels du secteur.

items.title: Les flux de pétrole du golfe Persique ont dépassé leur niveau pré-guerre
items.description: Selon les données compilées par Kpler, les flux pétroliers en provenance du Moyen-Orient ont dépassé leur niveau d’avant-guerre la semaine dernière : plus de 24 millions de barils par jour en moyenne ont été exportés, contre 23,3 millions avant le lancement par les États-Unis et Israël de la guerre contre l’Iran More Oil Is Now Coming Out of the Persian Gulf Than Before the Iran War », The Wall Street Journal , 20 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Cette hausse est visible depuis la fin de l’été. Celle-ci est attribuée par les analystes à plusieurs facteurs : l’escorte des navires commerciaux proposée aux armateurs par l’armée américaine, l’utilisation de pétroliers-navettes, qui traversent le détroit pour transborder par la suite leurs cargaisons vers d’autres navires dans le golfe d’Oman, et le contournement du détroit d’Ormuz via d’autres itinéraires qui contribuent à faire sortir le pétrole de la région, comme l’oléoduc saoudien Est-Ouest. D’autres dynamiques à l'œuvre pourraient également expliquer la hausse des flux. Selon des sources ayant une connaissance directe du sujet, l’Iran exporterait désormais une partie de son pétrole en passant par les Émirats arabes unis, dont la plupart des ports se situent à l’intérieur du golfe Persique. Ces derniers blanchiraient la provenance des barils, obtenant en retour un nouveau levier face à Téhéran ainsi qu’une nouvelle garantie de sécurité face à ce qui est perçu dans plusieurs États du Golfe comme un abandon des États-Unis. Après avoir lancé une guerre contre l’Iran, l’armée américaine a en effet échoué à protéger les villes et infrastructures énergétiques et civiles de ces pays, remettant en cause son système d’alliances. La hausse des flux, si elle est mesurable, n’a toutefois pas conduit à une baisse du prix du baril : le Brent a frôlé les 110 dollars par baril ces derniers jours, soit 70 % de plus qu’il y a un an. Le prix du baril de Brent reflète les tensions qui subsistent sur les marchés de l’énergie, et notamment la multiplication des attaques iraniennes contre les navires et le risque d’une reprise de la phase active du conflit après les élections de mi-mandat. Toutefois, le resserrement de l’écart entre le prix du baril de brut de Dubaï, la référence du pétrole moyen-oriental vendu en Asie, et le brut omanais, chargé hors du détroit d’Ormuz, laisse entrevoir une détente du marché physique. L’écart est tombé à 3,9 dollars par baril lundi 19 octobre, soit son niveau le plus bas depuis la fin du mois de juillet Key Mideast Oil Benchmark Hits 3-Month Low on Resilient Exports », Bloomberg , 21 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Au plus fort de la crise, en mars, lorsque Téhéran avait bloqué la plupart des transits via le détroit d’Ormuz, il avait dépassé les 60 dollars. L’article Les flux de pétrole du golfe Persique ont dépassé leur niveau pré-guerre est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: SITARAIL: le partenaire logistique de référence pour les chargeurs
items.description: Dans une interview, la Directrice commerciale de SITARAIL, Nadège Diarra Lompo, accordé en marge de la 5ᵉ édition du Translog Africa à Ouagadougou, a affirmé que « SITARAIL, avec l'appui des filiales de MSC telles qu'AGL, Côte d'Ivoire Terminal et Abidjan Terminal, réaffirme sa détermination à demeurer le partenaire logistique de référence pour les chargeurs de la sous-région. SITARAIL participe, aux côtés des filiales sœurs AGL Burkina, Côte d’Ivoire Terminal et Abidjan Terminal, à la 5ᵉ édition du Translog Africa à Ouagadougou. Que représente cet événement pour votre entreprise et dans quel esprit abordez-vous votre intervention ? Nadège DIARRA LOMPO (NDL) : La 5ᵉ édition de Translog Africa, organisée du 20 au 22 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou par le Conseil Burkinabè des Chargeurs (CBC) sous le Haut Patronage du Président du Faso, constitue une plateforme sous-régionale d'échange et de concertation stratégique majeure. Placé sous le thème central « Résilience et sécurisation des chaînes logistiques dans un environnement mondial en pleine mutation », ce symposium nous offre une tribune privilégiée pour intervenir sur la « Performance des corridors de transit vers les pays enclavés : enjeux des coûts, contraintes, gouvernance et coordination des acteurs ». C'est l'occasion pour nos filiales de réaffirmer notre volonté d'accompagner durablement le développement socio-économique des pays de l'hinterland à travers une chaîne logistique intégrée fluide, sûre et efficiente. Le thème de votre communication met l'accent sur les corridors de transit vers les pays enclavés. Quels sont aujourd'hui les principaux défis et contraintes identifiés sur le corridor Abidjan-Ouagadougou ? NDL : L'approvisionnement des pays sans littoral pose des défis logistiques et économiques majeurs, notamment l'éloignement des façades maritimes, la maîtrise des délais d'acheminement et la réduction de la part des coûts de transport dans le prix final des marchandises. Sur le corridor Abidjan-Ouagadougou, la performance globale dépend de notre capacité collective à lever les contraintes physiques et administratives : fluidifier les franchissements transfrontaliers, simplifier les procédures douanières et sécuriser les marchandises face aux aléas conjoncturels. C'est à cette condition que nous pourrons préserver la compétitivité des produits importés et des filières d'exportation. Dans ce contexte, quelle est la contribution spécifique du mode ferroviaire opéré par SITARAIL pour améliorer la compétitivité et la fluidité des flux ? NDL : Le chemin de fer est le vecteur par excellence du transport de masse en Afrique de l'Ouest. Grâce à sa capacité d’emport élevée sur une seule circulation, SITARAIL offre un report modal performant qui permet de réduire significativement les coûts à la tonne/kilomètre pour les chargeurs. En outre, le rail désengorge les axes routiers, préserve les infrastructures routières et réduit l’empreinte carbone globale du corridor. C'est une solution structurante, économique et durable pour acheminer les marchandises stratégiques, les conteneurs et les produits de première nécessité vers le Burkina Faso. Quels sont les récents investissements réalisés par SITARAIL pour moderniser son matériel et renforcer la performance de son réseau ? NDL : SITARAIL est engagée dans une dynamique continue de modernisation de son outil. Nos investissements stratégiques récents couvrent plusieurs volets essentiels : les renforcement et modernisation du parc de locomotives et acquisition de wagons adaptés aux besoins diversifiés des chargeurs ; l’équipement des ateliers de maintenance en outillages modernes pour garantir un taux de disponibilité élevé du matériel tout en facilitant le travail de nos techniciens ; le déploiement de systèmes avancés de sécurité ferroviaire et d'outils de suivi du trafic en temps réel pour offrir une traçabilité totale des cargaisons ; enfin, des programmes intensifs de formation continue pour nos agents et de création de nouvelles compétences aux standards internationaux du secteur afin de garantir la pérennité de l’activité. La gouvernance et la coordination des acteurs sont au cœur de votre sujet au Translog Africa. Quels leviers préconisez-vous pour optimiser cette synergie ? NDL : La performance d'un corridor ne repose pas uniquement sur les infrastructures, mais aussi sur l'harmonie entre ses acteurs. Il est indispensable pour nous de renforcer le dialogue permanent entre les administrations douanières, les autorités portuaires, les conseils des chargeurs comme le CBC et les transporteurs. Nous préconisons une gouvernance concertée axée sur la dématérialisation intégrale des procédures de transit, la mise en place de guichets uniques interconnectés et l'harmonisation des contrôles afin d'éliminer les goulots d'étranglement administratifs et de gagner en prédictibilité. SITARAIL s'inscrit au sein de l'écosystème du groupe MSC. Comment les synergies opérationnelles entre AGL, SITARAIL, Côte d'Ivoire Terminal et Abidjan Terminal renforcent-elles l'offre de service sur le corridor ? NDL : L'appartenance à la famille MSC nous permet d'offrir une solution intégrée de bout en bout d'une fluidité remarquable. Dès l'arrivée du navire au Port d'Abidjan, la synergie s'opère : Abidjan Terminal et Côte d'Ivoire Terminal assurent des opérations de manutention de classe mondiale avec des cadences de débarquement optimales. SITARAIL prend ensuite le relais direct sur le rail pour le pré/post-acheminement terrestre vers le Burkina Faso. Enfin, AGL (Africa Global Logistics) orchestre les prestations logistiques, de transit et de stockage dans l'hinterland. Cette complémentarité élimine les ruptures de charge et garantit un service continu, rapide et sécurisé pour l'ensemble des opérateurs économiques. Dans un environnement mondial et régional en pleine mutation, comment assurez-vous la résilience et la continuité opérationnelle du réseau ? NDL : La résilience repose sur l'anticipation, la flexibilité opérationnelle et la sécurisation. SITARAIL a renforcé le suivi géolocalisé de ses trains, optimisé la maintenance préventive des voies et mis en place des dispositifs de surveillance accrus sur l'ensemble du tracé. En travaillant en étroite synergie avec les autorités publiques et les forces de sécurité, nous veillons à maintenir la continuité territoriale des approvisionnements, indispensables à la stabilité et à la vitalité économique de nos pays. Quel est votre message clé à destination des chargeurs, des décideurs et des partenaires réunis à Ouagadougou lors de ce 5ᵉ Translog Africa ? NDL : Mon message est un message de confiance, d'engagement et de partenariat renforcé. SITARAIL, avec l'appui des filiales de MSC telles qu'AGL, Côte d'Ivoire Terminal et Abidjan Terminal, réaffirme sa détermination à demeurer le partenaire logistique de référence pour les chargeurs de la sous-région. En investissant continuellement dans nos équipements et en promouvant une gouvernance concertée avec des institutions majeures comme le CBC, nous continuons de faire du corridor Abidjan-Ouagadougou un moteur de croissance, d'intégration et de résilience pour l'Afrique de l'Ouest. Correspondance particulière L’article SITARAIL: le partenaire logistique de référence pour les chargeurs est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Inclusion financière : le Sénégal parmi les pays les plus avancés de l’UEMOA en 2025
items.description: Le Sénégal figure parmi les pays les plus avancés de l’UEMOA en matière d’inclusion financière en 2025, avec un indice synthétique de 0,651, supérieur à la moyenne régionale de 0,616. C’est ce qui ressort de l’analyse du rapport de l’évolution des indicateurs de suivi de l’inclusion financière dans l’UEMOA au titre de l’année 2025, rendu public le 20 octobre 2026, par la Banque centrale des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (BCEAO). L’inclusion financière a connu des avancées significatives ces dernières années au Sénégal. En fait, selon le rapport de l’évolution des indicateurs de suivi de l’inclusion financière dans l’Union économique et monétaire (UEMOA) au titre de l’année 2025, publié le mardi 20 octobre 2026, par la Banque centrale des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (BCEAO), le pays est parmi ceux qui ont le plus progressé pendant la période sous revue. En réalité les indicateurs clés en 2025 montrent que pour l’accès aux services financiers, il y a 150 points de service pour 10 000 adultes et 905 points pour 1 000 km². La monnaie électronique représente l’essentiel du réseau, avec 147,11 points pour 10 000 adultes. A lire aussi : Marché des titres de la dette publique : 1633,0 milliards levés en juin 2026 par les pays de l’Uemoa Concernant la bancarisation, le document de la BCEAO indique que le taux de bancarisation strict est de 27,42 %, tandis que la bancarisation élargie atteint 67,13 %, soit 16,56 points au-dessus de la moyenne UEMOA (50,57 %). Du côté de la microfinance au Sénégal, 39,71 % des adultes utilisent les services de microfinance, un niveau nettement supérieur à la moyenne régionale de 23,71 % pendant la période sous revue. Et pour la monnaie électronique, le taux d’utilisation atteint 66,29 %, au-dessus de la moyenne de l’Union qui est de 60,27 %. Globalement, selon les données de la BCEAO, le taux global d’utilisation des services financiers est de 102,73 % sur la base des comptes actifs. Corrigé de la multibancarité, il s’établit à 88,04 %, contre 76,06 % dans l’UEMOA. Évolution depuis 2015 En réalité, d’après la Banque centrale, l’indice d’inclusion financière est passé de 0,430 en 2015 à 0,651 en 2025, avec une progression presque continue depuis 2020. La bancarisation élargie a augmenté de 43,35 % à 67,13 % sur la période. « L’usage de la monnaie électronique a fortement progressé, de 17,83 % à 66,29 %. L’usage global corrigé de la multibancarité est passé de 52,43 % à 88,04 %, montrant une diffusion substantielle des services financiers auprès des adultes », rapporte la BCEAO. Coût des services bancaires Au-delà de la monnaie électronique, le document souligne également que le taux d’intérêt nominal des dépôts au niveau des banques est de 5,75 % et le taux réel de 4,29 %. Concernant les crédits, le taux d’intérêt nominal est de 5,98 % et le taux réel de 4,52 %. « Le Sénégal affiche ainsi le taux nominal de crédit le plus faible de l’UEMOA en 2025. Le profil du Sénégal associe une forte utilisation de la microfinance et du numérique à un coût du crédit relativement compétitif, malgré un recul de la densité totale des points de service par rapport à 2024 », montre le rapport. Mariama DIEME

Dr. Ayiku expressed appreciation to the company’s team and customers, emphasizing the organization’s commitment to delivering value and meeting homebuyers’ expectations. For prospective homeowners, LAKESIDE ESTATES remain your number choice in the real estate industry. items.description: The Member of Parliament for Bekwai, Ralph Poku-Adusei, has distributed 450 streetlights and 2,500 LED bulbs across the constituency under his “Let Bekwai Shine” initiative. The distribution, which took place on Sunday, October 18, covered all 34 electoral areas and schools, while the LED bulbs were allocated to tertiary and second-cycle institutions, hospitals, health centres and other key institutions. Mr Poku-Adusei said the initiative was in response to calls from constituents for additional streetlights and LED bulbs to improve visibility and security in their communities. He explained that the installation of the lighting facilities was intended to brighten the constituency and reduce incidents of crime and attacks carried out under the cover of darkness. According to the MP, improved lighting would also help residents and businesses carry out their activities more safely, while supporting economic activity across the constituency. “Bekwai must shine!” he said, describing the initiative as part of his broader vision to make the constituency self-sufficient. The intervention is expected to improve lighting in public spaces and key institutions, with the distribution of streetlights across all 34 electoral areas aimed at extending the benefits to communities throughout the constituency.

items.title: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in alleged CCD encounter
items.description: The suspect accused of running over and fatally injuring a 14-year-old boy in Multan was killed in an alleged encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur early on Wednesday, police said. The suspect, identified as Tauqeer, had allegedly escaped from police custody while on remand, a CCD spokesperson said. A Multan court on Tuesday granted police three-day physical remand of the suspect. The suspect was accused of hitting the victim, who used to work for him, with his car in a private housing society. He was arrested on Monday and presented before Judicial Magistrate Saadia Aslam on Tuesday. According to the spokesperson, the CCD personnel attempted to stop two individuals riding a motorcycle on Bahawalpur’s Northern Bypass when an exchange of fire ensued, leaving the suspect dead. On Tuesday, police requested a 14-day physical remand of the suspect for investigation. However, the judicial magistrate granted the police a three-day remand. At the time, Multan City Police Officer (CPO) Akhtar Farooq said while speaking to the media that raids were being conducted for the arrest of a second suspect. “We all are in deep pain,” the CPO said, adding that the orphan boy had been “subjected to barbarity”. The CCTV footage of the incident shows a boy running on the road after spotting a car. The car is seen swerving and chasing the boy, eventually hitting him. The boy, who fell, then rams into the gate of a nearby house and dies on impact. A case was registered on the state’s behalf at Multan’s DHA police station. The first information report (FIR) named two suspects and invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. According to the FIR, the teenage boy had been working for the suspects and was being trained as an electrician. His cousin told police that the boy had reportedly faced violence and threats by the suspects, the FIR said, adding that the 14-year-old was fleeing when the suspects pursued him in a car and hit him. Police arrested one of the suspects while the other escaped, the FIR stated. It added that their vehicle had been taken into custody.

items.title: Elon Musk ordered reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine – Report
items.description: Elon Musk ordered a reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday, after the tech billionaire said any limits on the SpaceX-operated communications system would ultimately have come from the president. Musk capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, making some of Kyiv’s drones useless, the Journal reported, citing anonymous US officials and people familiar with the matter. Kyiv has accused Washington of deliberately slowing speeds at which Starshield can be used effectively — a charge denied last week by US President Donald Trump. Musk had previously said that “any limits on speed or usage” of Starshield systems were “decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” referring to Trump. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Washington had no prior knowledge of the slowdown. “The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk,” Rubio said during his trip to India. “That’s a private company; the president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything… I’m telling you, there was no foreknowledge.” On Tuesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said that the Pentagon had not directed any changes to Starshield, saying: “We haven’t pulled anything back.” “Nothing’s changed from our view. We haven’t made any directives or anything like that,” he said. Trump said last week he did not request any curbs to Starshield, adding: “It wasn’t me. And I don’t think it was Elon.” Kyiv last week reported restrictions to the service, which it sees as crucial to fending off Moscow’s invasion, shortly after Trump criticized Ukraine and urged it to stop targeting Russian oil refineries. Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink’s military-grade satellite service, for its battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russia-occupied territory, and its interceptor drones. It also uses SpaceX’s parallel Starlink civilian satellite system. Relations between Washington and Kyiv have been increasingly tense in recent days, with Trump calling for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to be replaced after he criticized a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets. items.title: Fasoranti was true custodian of Awoism, not slogan chaser — Yoruba Group
items.description: …Death ends extraordinary chapter in Yorubaland’s political history By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Conscience of Yoruba Nation Group has mourned the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, describing his passing as the end of an extraordinary chapter in the political history of Yorubaland and Nigeria. The convener of the group, Abagun Kole Omololu, in a statement, said the organisation received with profound sorrow the news of the death of Fasoranti, whom he described as a steadfast adherent of Awoism and a committed custodian of its ideals. Omololu said: “His death marks the end of an extraordinary chapter in the political history of Yorubaland and Nigeria. “With his departure, we have lost a man whose life was defined by an uncommon devotion to principle, an abiding commitment to public service and an unwavering belief in the progressive ideals of Chief Obafemi Awolowo. “Pa Fasoranti was not merely a follower of Awolowo; he was a steadfast adherent of Awoism and one of its most committed custodians. “To him, Awoism was neither a convenient political slogan nor a political legacy to be exploited for personal gain. “It represented a philosophy of governance founded on education, social justice, accountable leadership, genuine federalism and the welfare of ordinary citizens.” He said Fasoranti’s service as an educationist, his tenure as Commissioner for Finance in the old Ondo State under the progressive administration of Chief Michael Adekunle Ajasin, and his decades of involvement in Afenifere reflected his consistent commitment to those ideals. Omololu added that Fasoranti remained committed to the belief that political leadership should be judged by its contributions to society rather than the privileges attached to public office. He said the late elder statesman’s integrity stood in contrast to a political culture in which principles were often sacrificed for expediency. “Pa Fasoranti’s integrity and steadfastness offer a powerful contrast to a political culture in which principles are too often sacrificed at the altar of expediency. “He belonged to a generation that understood that public office was a trust, political conviction a responsibility, and honesty an indispensable attribute of leadership. “His example reminds us that integrity is demonstrated not by what people proclaim, but by the principles they uphold when compromise would be more convenient. “His advocacy of democratic governance and genuine federalism also reflected his understanding that Nigeria’s stability and prosperity depend on justice, equity and respect for the legitimate aspirations of its constituent peoples,” he said. According to Omololu, Fasoranti’s death should serve as both a moment of mourning and an opportunity for reflection on the ideals he upheld. “For the Conscience of Yoruba Nation Group, his passing is both a moment of grief and a solemn call to reflection. “Awoism must not be reduced to the celebration of Awolowo’s name or the recitation of his achievements. Its authenticity must be measured by the quality of governance, access to education, protection of the vulnerable and the willingness of leaders to place the common good above personal interests.” The group extended its condolences to the Fasoranti family, Afenifere, the people of Akure and Ondo State, and the Yoruba nation. Omololu said the late Afenifere leader’s ideals would endure beyond his death, urging political leaders and others to preserve the principles of justice, integrity and public welfare associated with Awoism. “Pa Fasoranti has departed, but the ideals to which he devoted his life endure. “The most fitting tribute to his memory is to uphold the principles he cherished and ensure that Awoism remains a living commitment to justice, integrity and the welfare of our people. “May his soul rest in perfect peace,” he added. items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Aligning Resources with Strategic Ambition.
items.description: Insight An organisation cannot achieve its strategic ambitions if its resources remain tied to outdated priorities. CEOs must ensure that budgets, talent, technology, and operational capacity are aligned with the results the organisation intends to deliver. Resource allocation is not simply an annual budgeting exercise. It is an ongoing leadership responsibility that requires difficult choices, regular performance reviews, and a willingness to redirect resources when circumstances change. Key Strategies: 1. Map available resources against the organization’s strategic priorities. 2. Identify capability gaps that could prevent successful execution. 3. Prioritize investments based on strategic value and expected returns. 4. Reduce spending on activities that no longer justify their resource requirements. 5. Review resource allocation as performance, risks, and opportunities evolve. CEO Leadership Actions. Require each major strategic initiative to have a realistic resource plan. Identify areas where investment is insufficient or resources are being underused. Ensure that resource allocation decisions reflect strategic priorities rather than historical budgets alone. Actionable Tip. * Ask: “If we were allocating our resources from scratch today, would we distribute them in the same way?” Why This Matters? Strategic ambition without appropriate resources remains an aspiration. When CEOs align investment and organizational capacity with priorities, they improve execution, strengthen financial discipline, and increase the likelihood of achieving meaningful results. About the Author Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.
